items.title: Florida pastor found guilty over role in assassination of Haitian president
items.summary: Christian Emmanuel Sanon is convicted of involvement in the plot that resulted in the killing of Jovenel Moïse.
items.body:
Image source, Police Nationale Haiti

Image caption,

Christian Emmanuel Sanon was found guilty of all eight counts against him in a Florida court on Wednesday

ByAleks Phillips

A Florida pastor has been found guilty of a number of charges relating to the assassination of the Haitian President Jovenel Moïse.

Christian Emmanuel Sanon, a dual US-Haitian national, was convicted of all eight charges against him, including conspiracy to kill or kidnap a person. He faces a potential sentence of life in prison.

The 67-year-old was accused of being involved in a plot to replace Moïse as Haiti's president with himself in 2021, allegedly so he could award lucrative contracts to a Florida-based security outfit once in place.

The murder of Moïse has left Haiti without a leader for five years. That political vacuum has intensified gang violence in the impoverished Caribbean nation.

A presidential election is scheduled for next year and Moïse's wife, Martine, who was injured in the attack that killed her husband, announced this week that she intended to stand.

Sanon was found guilty on Wednesday following an eight-week trial in federal court in Miami, according to CBS, the BBC's US partner. His lawyer said he maintains his innocence and that he intends to appeal against the verdict, it reports.

Prosecutors said Sanon had "political aspirations" in Haiti and, in April 2021, met several other co-conspirators to devise a plan to oust Moïse in an armed raid on the presidential palace in the capital, Port-au-Prince.

Among them were the heads of the companies Counter Terrorist Unit Federal Academy and Counter Terrorist Unit Security - collectively referred to as CTU - who would finance the coup in exchange for government contracts for infrastructure projects, and to provide security forces and equipment.

A few months later, the other conspirators realised that Sanon had "neither the constitutional qualifications nor the popular support" to become Haiti's president and so shifted to another candidate, the US Department of Justice said.

At the same time, the plot had developed from one to forcibly remove Moïse from office to assassinating him, investigators said.

Dozens of people have been implicated in the conspiracy, which prosecutors said involved co-ordinating funding for and delivering weapons and mercenaries to Haiti to carry out the attack.

On 6 July that year, a group of Colombian mercenaries entered the presidential palace and killed Moïse. His wife, who was also injured in the attack, said at the time that the assailants had "riddled" her husband with bullets.

Image source, Getty Images

Image caption,

Jovenel Moïse was gunned down by mercenaries in Haiti's presidential palace in 2021

The successful assassination plot raised questions in Haiti about the relative ease with which the mercenaries were able to gain access to the president.

The country - the poorest in the Americas - has been ravaged by gang violence for years, but Moïse's assassination ushered in a period of worsening instability that emboldened gangs and prompted the deployment of a multinational force.

However, this has struggled to penetrate areas where gangs hold sway and more than 5,700 people have been killed or injured in the year to 11 September, the UN said last month.

Sanon and several other co-conspirators were arrested by Haitian authorities, while three mercenaries were killed in a gun battle with police. Eighteen people were transferred to Florida in September to stand trial over the plot.

Four men, including the heads of the CTU, were convicted of their role earlier this year. Sanon had been scheduled to be tried with them, but his case was delayed due to health reasons, according to CBS.

Sanon was born in Haiti but moved to the US as a teenager. He told the court he had worked in churches in Haitian immigrant communities in several parts of the US including Florida, US media report.

blocks.text: 图片来源：海地国家警察（Police Nationale Haiti）
图片说明，
周三，克里斯蒂安·埃马纽埃尔·萨农在佛罗里达州一家法院被判全部八项罪名成立
作者：Aleks Phillips
一名佛罗里达牧师被判与海地总统朱弗内尔·莫伊兹遇刺案相关的多项罪名成立。
美海双重国籍的克里斯蒂安·埃马纽埃尔·萨农被判全部八项罪名成立，其中包括密谋杀害或绑架他人。他可能面临终身监禁。
这名67岁男子被指控于2021年参与密谋取代莫伊兹、由自己出任海地总统，据称目的是在上台后把利润丰厚的合同授予一家总部位于佛罗里达的安保公司。
莫伊兹遇刺使海地五年没有领导人。这一政治真空加剧了这个贫困加勒比国家的黑帮暴力。
总统选举定于明年举行，莫伊兹的妻子马丁在丈夫遇袭中受伤，她本周宣布有意参选。
据CBS（BBC的美国合作伙伴）报道，萨农周三在迈阿密联邦法院经过为期八周的审理后被判有罪。报道称，他的律师说他坚称自己无罪，并打算对判决提出上诉。
检方称，萨农在海地有“政治抱负”，并于2021年4月与其他几名同谋会面，策划武装突袭首都太子港的总统府，以推翻莫伊兹。
其中就包括 Counter Terrorist Unit Federal Academy 和 Counter Terrorist Unit Security 两家公司的负责人——它们被统称为 CTU——他们将为政变提供资金，以换取基础设施项目的政府合同，并提供安保力量和装备。
美国司法部表示，几个月后，其他同谋意识到萨农“既不具备宪法规定的资格，也没有民意支持”来担任海地总统，于是转向另一名候选人。
调查人员说，与此同时，该计划已从强行将莫伊兹赶下台演变成刺杀他。
数十人被指卷入这起阴谋。检方称，该阴谋包括筹集资金，并向海地运送武器和雇佣兵以实施袭击。
当年7月6日，一群哥伦比亚雇佣兵进入总统府并杀害了莫伊兹。同样在袭击中受伤的他的妻子当时说，袭击者朝她丈夫“打得像筛子一样”。

blocks.alt: Jovenel Moïse sits at a desk with his fingers intertwined.

blocks.text: 图片来源：Getty Images
图片说明，
2021年，朱弗内尔·莫伊兹在海地总统府遭雇佣兵枪杀
这次刺杀阴谋得手后，海地有人质疑雇佣兵为何能如此轻易接近总统。
这个美洲最贫穷的国家多年来一直饱受黑帮暴力摧残，但莫伊兹遇刺开启了一段更趋动荡的时期，使黑帮更加猖獗，并促使一支多国部队被部署到位。
不过，这一努力难以进入黑帮控制的地区；联合国上月表示，截至9月11日的一年里，已有超过5700人被杀害或受伤。
萨农和其他几名同谋被海地当局逮捕，另有三名雇佣兵在与警方的枪战中被打死。9月，18人被移交至佛罗里达，就这起阴谋接受审判。
包括反恐部队（CTU）负责人在内的四名男子今年早些时候已因其角色被定罪。据CBS报道，萨农原定与他们一同受审，但因健康原因案件被推迟。
萨农出生于海地，十几岁时移居美国。美国媒体报道，他告诉法庭，他曾在包括佛罗里达在内的美国多地海地移民社区的教堂工作。

items.title: 'Frustrated' - Democrats remain a divided party despite winning big in midterms
items.summary: After winning power in Congress, a Democratic conference in Denver was animated with talk on the best way forward.
items.body:
Image source, Mark Makela/Getty Images

Image caption,

More than 2,000 people gathered in Denver for a What's Next? Democrat event

BySheila Flynn

Senior US Reporter, Reporting fromDenver, Colorado

When James Talarico - who recently became the first Democrat to win election to the US Senate for Texas since 1988 - appeared onstage at a Democratic political conference, he was greeted by a chorus of cheers and a standing ovation.

But the audience's enthusiasm dimmed when he suggested working in tandem with the Republican Trump administration.

"We should make the final two years of his presidency the most productive of any presidency in American history," said Talarico, who at 37 will become the youngest member of the Senate when he takes his oath of office in January. "Because this moment is so much bigger and so much more important than the red team or the blue team."

He was just one of many rising stars speaking last week during a political conference in Denver, titled "What's Next: investigating strategies and priorities for the future of the Democratic Party".

And the answer to what's next? No one's sure.

Image source, Reuters

Image caption,

Texas Democrat James Talarico got a mixed reaction in the room when he pushed the party to work with President Trump

Those present, who included activists and political organisers, were invigorated and celebratory the week after a "blue tsunami" saw Democrats win in Republican heartlands in the midterm elections.

The party took control of both chambers of Congress, winning a majority in the House by over 80 seats and gaining nine seats in the Senate.

But the atmosphere in Denver was also introspective and forward-looking, as discussions focused on how those victories were won, which issues did not resonate, and what would be needed to continue the party's seat-winning momentum.

Some, like Talarico, suggested working alongside Republicans to push forward an economic agenda that would resonate with Americans, such as extending health coverage and reducing inflation.

Alabama Congressman Shomari Figures - who surprised many pollsters when he held his seat despite Republicans redrawing his district months before the election - cautioned against going after Trump, when there were more pressing concerns for Americans.

Previous Democratic-led efforts to impeach Trump both ended in Senate acquittals.

"We impeached him twice and got him back - with a Republican majority," Figures said.

Yet others, like Maryland Congresswoman Angela Alsobrooks, insisted that voters wanted to see accountability.

Voters "realised the smash-and-grab that occurred, and they want people to account for it", she said, pushing for transparent investigations into the Trump administration.

The two-day event was staged by Majority Democrats, a political action committee launched last year to address tensions between the left and centrist factions of the party, with some of the biggest divisions forming over how to deliver health care and the war in Gaza.

Prominent left-wing members of the party - such as Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Senator-elect Abdul El Sayed - were not in attendance.

Image caption,

Protesters Vicki Saxe and Tami Butters were demanding Democratic Party change

In Denver, it was clear those tensions weren't going away, as protesters waving Palestinian flags shouted as people walked past and armed police looked on.

Some in attendance made a point to criticise Chuck Schumer, the long-time Democratic Senate minority leader who is seen as a part of the party's centrist establishment.

He has been challenged for the role of Senate majority leader by Chris Van Hollen, a senator from Maryland who is considered a left-wing populist.

Democrats have not been "strong enough in their displeasure with what's been happening with Trump, and I think that's one of the reasons that people are asking for new leadership," said Vicki Saxe, holding a sign criticising Schumer.

"I'm frustrated with the lack of urgency that I feel coming from the party leadership," said Tami Butters, 65, standing beside her with a "Vote Yes for Chris Van Hollen" sign. She cited the absence of 11 Democrats last week, when the House voted on whether to consider impeaching US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. The effort failed.

Hakeem Jeffries, a centrist Democrat who is poised to become the country's first black speaker of the House, faced similar pushback, as protesters heckled his speech.

One of the biggest issues of division is the war in Gaza, with both Schumer and Jeffries backing continued military assistance for Israel, while some new members of Congress, like El-Sayed, support ending unconditional US military aid to Israel.

Non-profit founder Shiva Saram, who also chairs the Iranian American Legal Defense Fund, travelled from Connecticut to the conference despite having "almost left my party over Gaza and the Iran War".

Image source, Reuters

Image caption,

Protesters interrupted New York Congressman Hakeem Jeffries at the event

Saram has been newly encouraged, however, by the "real depth in our bench of new and young leaders".

"What my party has done wrong for too long is we did not listen," she said.

Many speakers and guests stressed that the Democrats won because they focused on real policies that would impact their constituents' daily lives - and that failing to do so in previous years might have been why they lost on those occasions.

Delaware Senator Chris Coons told BBC News that he had advised newly elected members to "under-promise and over-deliver".

"We got hired because the average American wants us to help make their lives better - lower their costs, end the cruelty and the corruption and give them more reason for hope," he said. "That's going to require hard work, and it isn't going to be easy to get done."

Michigan Representative Kristen McDonald Rivet agreed, saying she did not care "if we have to put Donald Trump's name" on legislation to gain the president's support for efforts to help her district.

Image caption,

Texan Carlos Repetto-Ayala (L) wants Democrats to be "laser-focused" on issues that voters truly care about

Tahra Hoops, the 28-year-old senior director of economic analysis at the Chamber of Progress, a "left-of-centre" tech think tank, suggested that the party's divisions be embraced, not paved over.

"I think Democrats can look different wherever they are," she said.

While "very progressive" candidates can win in her home town of New York City, she said it made sense that Talarico held more centrist views because running in Texas "is not going to be the same".

"America is a very diverse country; our politicians and their views should also be diverse," she added.

Carlos Repetto-Ayala, a campaign consultant, made a similar point. The 25-year-old Texan travelled with two friends to the What's Next? event, wearing a cowboy hat and a red-white-and-blue pin on his lapel in the shape of the Lone Star State.

"It is a big tent party, but I think, as long as everyone that's in the party is laser-focused on addressing the issues that people would like for them to fix, I think Democrats will be successful," he said.

items.title: Indian driver wins $1.3m in life-changing lottery prize
items.summary: A truck driver's fortunes have changed overnight after he won a Diwali lottery in the northern Indian state of Punjab.
items.body:
Indian driver wins $1.3m in life-changing lottery prize

Indian driver wins $1.3m in life-changing lottery prize

Baljinder Singh, a truck driver from the northern Indian state of Punjab, has won a 120m rupee [£978,000; $1.3m] lottery with a ticket that cost him just 500 rupees. But Singh says the big win won't change his life. He plans to carry on working as a truck driver. Meanwhile, celebrations are under way at his home, with family members distributing sweets to mark the win.

Mark Speakman has said he will not contest his south Sydney seat of Cronulla at next year’s state election. Photograph: Bianca de Marchi/AAP

Mark Speakman has said he will not contest his south Sydney seat of Cronulla at next year’s state election. Photograph: Bianca de Marchi/AAP

Mark Speakman resigns and says Liberals face ‘existential threat’ as NSW exodus continues

Former NSW opposition leader warns party against becoming ‘Labor lite’ or ‘One Nation lite’ in late-night speech

• Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Former New South Wales opposition leader, Mark Speakman, will not contest his seat at the March state election, the latest in a mass exodus of MPs under the Liberal leader who replaced him, Kellie Sloane.

In a late-night speech on Thursday, the final sitting day of NSW’s legislative assembly ahead of the vote, Speakman said he would not contest his south Sydney seat of Cronulla, which he has held since 2011.

blocks.text: 新南威尔士州前反对党领袖马克·斯皮克曼将不在 3 月州选举中竞选连任，这是在接替他的自由党领袖凯莉·斯隆任内议员大规模出走的最新一例。
周四是新南威尔士州议会立法大会投票前的最后一个开会日，斯皮克曼在深夜演讲中表示，他将不再竞选自 2011 年起一直担任的悉尼南部克罗纳拉选区议席。

他是现任 24 名自由党议员中第 8 位宣布不在 3 月竞选连任的人，此前已有乔丹·莱恩、马克·库尔、塔尼娅·戴维斯、雷·威廉姆斯、詹姆斯·格里芬、马克·泰勒和阿利斯特·亨斯肯斯。
这一宣布几乎就在斯皮克曼在党内倒戈中辞去反对党领袖、由斯隆不战而胜当选一年之际。
《悉尼晨锋报》Resolve 民调显示，同期联盟党在新南威尔士州的第一偏好票已从 28% 降至 23%。
工党支持率已从 37% 降至 30%，而 Resolve 直到 3 月才开始单独民调的一国党目前为 26%。
上周，斯隆表示其政党不会与一国党联合组阁，但并未排除信心与供给协议。《澳大利亚金融评论报》报道称，她的许多议员私下预计自由党将与一国党组成联盟。
在议会任期即将结束的演讲中，作为党内温和派成员的斯皮克曼警告自由党不要变成“精简版工党”或“精简版一国党”，称他们应坚持“孟席斯自由主义”的价值观。
斯皮克曼在提及宝琳·汉森的“单一文化”说法时表示，澳大利亚是“地球上最成功的多元文化社会”，并且“因此更加美好”。
他说：“你知道，我们听到有些人说我们想要单一文化，而不支持这种单一文化的人似乎就是澳大利亚的敌人、仇恨澳大利亚。”
“我热爱澳大利亚的多元文化。多样性是我们的优势。这是我们的优势，我们应该在此基础上继续发展。”
身为大律师的斯皮克曼于 2015 至 2017 年担任环境部长，并于 2017 年至佩罗泰特政府在 2023 年选举中败选期间担任总检察长。
佩罗泰特辞职后，他被选为自由党及反对党领袖，并担任该职至去年 11 月。
周四他说，反对党领袖“常被称为政坛最艰难的工作”，虽然对他而言“最终还是瓦解了”，但他大部分时间领导的反对党“在民调中能与政府抗衡，甚至领先”。
他表示，自己担任总检察长期间的政绩包括立法使新南威尔士州成为澳大利亚首个将强制控制入罪的司法管辖区，在刑事性侵审判中引入肯定性同意标准，并改革刑事与民事儿童性侵案件处理。
斯皮克曼的辞职结束了周四他在质询时间发言后再次升温的猜测，这对斯隆是最新一次打击；他在离职演讲中称斯隆“具备成为杰出州长的特质”。
周四早些时候，新南威尔士州州长克里斯·明恩斯宣布，前自由党议员及议会工作人员塔尼娅·拉富尔将作为工党候选人竞逐自由党占据的埃平选区。

Guardian Australia has been awarded two Walkley awards for excellence in journalism. Composite: Mike Bowers/David L Kelly/The Guardian

Guardian Australia takes home two Walkley awards for excellence in journalism

Stories revealing Pauline Hanson’s US trip with Gina Rinehart and the systematic betrayal of Kardell Lomas before her death recognised

Guardian Australia journalists have won two Walkley awards, one for a story about the systematic betrayal of a woman who was killed by her partner, and another for an exclusive story that revealed Pauline Hanson had travelled to the US with mining billionaire Gina Rinehart.

Investigative reporter Sarah Martin won the award for print/text news report for her exclusive story that revealed the One Nation leader and her chief of staff, James Ashby, travelled with Rinehart on the mining magnate’s Gulfstream 700 on 27 October last year.

The pair stayed at Rinehart’s Palm Beach mansion, close to US president Donald Trump’s Mar-a-Lago resort.

After Guardian Australia published details of Hanson’s flight, her office lodged an amendment to the registrar of senators’ interests declaring the sponsored travel.

Queensland correspondent Ben Smee and the Guardian team won the award for coverage of Indigenous affairs for the story of the betrayal of Kardell Lomas, who repeatedly sought help – from domestic violence support services and the police – to escape the violent and dangerous man who killed her.

Lomas had 24 interactions with various agencies – and she repeatedly disclosed fears for her safety, death threats, serious violence and other abuse.

Ben Smee and the Guardian team were awarded a Walkley award for their coverage of the lead up to Kardell Lomas’s death. Composite: Victoria Hart/Guardian Design

Smee and Martin were finalists in two other categories, Martin for ‘Inside One Nation’ and Smee for his feature “‘Starting to frighten me’: the final weeks of Hannah Clarke’s life”.

Business editor Jonathan Barrett was also a finalist, in the print/text feature writing category, for his story “‘A child goes to bed and doesn’t wake up’: the families left in shock after the sudden death of their healthy children”.

The 2026 Walkley print/text award for feature writing under 4,000 words was awarded to the Australian Financial Review’s Sam Buckingham-Jones for the story “Maccas in a Rolls: inside Kyle Sandilands’ pivot to $100 tradie plans”.

For feature writing over 4,000 words, the Age and The Sydney Morning Herald’s Melissa Fyfe and Carla Hildebrandt took home the award for their story “Virginia: the Final Chapter”.

The scoop of the year was awarded to the ABC team behind “Bondi: what ASIO knew”, which included Sean Rubinsztein-Dunlop, Olivia Caisley, and Michael Workman.

Tony Wright, an associate editor and special writer for The Age and The Sydney Morning Herald, took home the award for outstanding contribution to journalism.

items.body:
Sarah Venter, founder of the Baobab Foundation, with one of the baobabs to be transported to Timbavati reserve in north-eastern South Africa. Photograph: Courtesy of Timbavati nature reserve

Sarah Venter, founder of the Baobab Foundation, with one of the baobabs to be transported to Timbavati reserve in north-eastern South Africa. Photograph: Courtesy of Timbavati nature reserve

Race to replant five South African baobabs after export blocked

The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits

Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.

The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa, on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover. The trees had been stranded at a warehouse in Durban since July, when they were intercepted by authorities who said they had been moved without the necessary permissions.

The department of forestry, fisheries and the environment confirmed the trees had been destined for Georgia but did not name the buyer.

The case echoes an episode in Kenya four years ago, when eight baobabs were uprooted to be exported to Shekvetili Dendrological Park, owned by Bidzina Ivanishvili, an influential Georgian billionaire and the country’s former prime minister. Ivanishvili has filled the park with ancient, giant trees from Georgia, transporting them by boat along the Black Sea.

The export of the Kenyan baobabs was initially blocked after an outcry by environmentalists, who condemned their export as biopiracy, but later allowed to go ahead.

Otherwise, such exports are very rare, say experts. David Newton, programme office director for east and southern Africa for Traffic, an NGO that monitors the trade in wild animals and plants, said: “It is very unusual to see baobabs being used as ornamental plants … mainly because they are exceptionally difficult to dig out of the ground and transport, and then to successfully re-establish.”

Sarah Venter, founder of the Baobab Foundation, who has led efforts to replant the South African trees, said she believes they have a good chance of surviving if they are replanted quickly. The winter months of May to October, when the trees lose their leaves and are dormant, is a good time to move them.

“As soon as spring starts [in November], the trees use their water to flush their new leaves, and that’s when we need to get them into the ground as soon as possible,” she said.

The rescue mission has faced delays because of the challenges associated with moving such large trees, which are transported on special trucks capable of carrying abnormal loads. The five baobabs weigh between 19 and 29 tonnes, have a diameter of up to 4.5 metres (15ft) and a height of up to 12.5 metres.

Baobabs, known as the tree of life, are protected under South African law, which means a permit is required to cut or disturb them.

“A baobab isn’t just part of an ecosystem, it is an ecosystem in itself,” said Wambui Ippolito, a landscape designer, lecturer and horticulturist from Kenya. “These trees are biodiversity anchors.”

Animals ranging from bats and bush babies, to grey-headed parrots and the southern ground hornbill shelter in its cavities, while elephants, monkeys and warthogs feast on its fruit.

The trees have huge cultural importance, added Ippolito. “It has always been a sacred tree in Africa. It doesn’t matter where you go: Senegal, Mali, Ghana – wherever you go, if there is a community around a baobab tree, that tree is sacred,” she said. “Somebody’s great-great-great-great-great-grandparents sat under that tree, and it is part of human history in that area.”

Baobabs have shallow roots, which means they do not need to be planted very deeply, and these regrow fairly quickly, said Venter. Once replanted, the trees will be stabilised with cables and protected by electric fences to prevent damage from elephants.

The trees are thought to be between 200 and 300 years old. “Baobabs easily reach 1,000 years old, so they’ve got a few hundred years ahead of them if they survive,” said Venter.

A criminal case has been opened against the owner of a landscaping company allegedly responsible for the illegal harvesting and transportation of the trees.

Sarah Venter, founder of the Baobab Foundation, with one of the baobabs to be transported to Timbavati reserve in north-eastern South Africa. Photograph: Courtesy of Timbavati nature reserve
Race to replant five South African baobabs after export blocked
The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits
Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.

The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa, on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover. The trees had been stranded at a warehouse in Durban since July, when they were intercepted by authorities who said they had been moved without the necessary permissions.
The department of forestry, fisheries and the environment confirmed the trees had been destined for Georgia but did not name the buyer.

The case echoes an episode in Kenya four years ago, when eight baobabs were uprooted to be exported to Shekvetili Dendrological Park, owned by Bidzina Ivanishvili, an influential Georgian billionaire and the country’s former prime minister. Ivanishvili has filled the park with ancient, giant trees from Georgia, transporting them by boat along the Black Sea.
The export of the Kenyan baobabs was initially blocked after an outcry by environmentalists, who condemned their export as biopiracy, but later allowed to go ahead.

Otherwise, such exports are very rare, say experts. David Newton, programme office director for east and southern Africa for Traffic, an NGO that monitors the trade in wild animals and plants, said: “It is very unusual to see baobabs being used as ornamental plants … mainly because they are exceptionally difficult to dig out of the ground and transport, and then to successfully re-establish.”

Sarah Venter, founder of the Baobab Foundation, who has led efforts to replant the South African trees, said she believes they have a good chance of surviving if they are replanted quickly. The winter months of May to October, when the trees lose their leaves and are dormant, is a good time to move them.
“As soon as spring starts [in November], the trees use their water to flush their new leaves, and that’s when we need to get them into the ground as soon as possible,” she said.

The rescue mission has faced delays because of the challenges associated with moving such large trees, which are transported on special trucks capable of carrying abnormal loads. The five baobabs weigh between 19 and 29 tonnes, have a diameter of up to 4.5 metres (15ft) and a height of up to 12.5 metres.
Baobabs, known as the tree of life, are protected under South African law, which means a permit is required to cut or disturb them.
“A baobab isn’t just part of an ecosystem, it is an ecosystem in itself,” said Wambui Ippolito, a landscape designer, lecturer and horticulturist from Kenya. “These trees are biodiversity anchors.”
Animals ranging from bats and bush babies, to grey-headed parrots and the southern ground hornbill shelter in its cavities, while elephants, monkeys and warthogs feast on its fruit.

The trees have huge cultural importance, added Ippolito. “It has always been a sacred tree in Africa. It doesn’t matter where you go: Senegal, Mali, Ghana – wherever you go, if there is a community around a baobab tree, that tree is sacred,” she said. “Somebody’s great-great-great-great-great-grandparents sat under that tree, and it is part of human history in that area.”

Baobabs have shallow roots, which means they do not need to be planted very deeply, and these regrow fairly quickly, said Venter. Once replanted, the trees will be stabilised with cables and protected by electric fences to prevent damage from elephants.
The trees are thought to be between 200 and 300 years old. “Baobabs easily reach 1,000 years old, so they’ve got a few hundred years ahead of them if they survive,” said Venter.
A criminal case has been opened against the owner of a landscaping company allegedly responsible for the illegal harvesting and transportation of the trees.

五棵南非猴面包树出口受阻后，人们争分夺秒重新栽种
这些树原计划卖给格鲁吉亚一名未具名买家，据报在没有必要许可的情况下被挖出
南非环保人士正在争分夺秒地补种五棵有数百年树龄的猴面包树。这些重达20吨的树被一名出口商挖出，试图运往数千英里外的格鲁吉亚。
这些猴面包树周三抵达南非东北部廷巴瓦蒂的一处保护区，将在那里重新栽种，并用缆绳固定以帮助它们恢复。自7月被当局截获并称其在没有必要许可的情况下被转移以来，这些树一直滞留在德班的一座仓库里。
林业、渔业与环境部门证实这些树原定运往格鲁吉亚，但并未公布买家姓名。
此案与四年前肯尼亚的一起事件相似：当时有八棵猴面包树被连根挖起，准备出口到由有影响力的格鲁吉亚亿万富豪、该国前总理比济纳·伊万尼什维利拥有的 Shekvetili Dendrological Park。伊万尼什维利用沿黑海运输的方式，把格鲁吉亚的古老巨树填满了这座园林。
肯尼亚猴面包树的出口起初因环保人士强烈反对而被叫停，他们谴责这是生物剽窃，但后来仍获准放行。
专家表示，除此之外，这类出口非常罕见。监测野生动植物贸易的非政府组织 Traffic 东非和南部非洲项目办公室主任戴维·牛顿说：“把猴面包树当作观赏植物来用是非常罕见的……主要是因为把它们从地里挖出来并运输极其困难，而且还要成功重新栽活。”
带领补种南非这些树木的猴面包树基金会创始人萨拉·文特说，她相信如果尽快重新栽种，它们很有希望存活。5月至10月的冬季，树木落叶进入休眠，是搬运它们的好时机。
她说：“春天一开始（11月），这些树就会用水分抽出新叶，那时我们必须尽快把它们种进土里。”
由于搬运如此巨大的树木面临种种困难，救援行动出现了延误，这些树需要用能够运载超限货物的特种卡车运输。这五棵猴面包树重达19至29吨，直径最可达4.5米（15英尺），高度最可达12.5米。
猴面包树被称为生命之树，受南非法律保护，砍伐或扰动它们需要许可证。
来自肯尼亚的景观设计师、讲师兼园艺师万布伊·伊波利托说：“猴面包树不只是生态系统的一部分，它本身就是一个生态系统。这些树是生物多样性的支柱。”
从蝙蝠、丛婴猴，到灰头鹦鹉和南非地犀鸟，都会在它的树洞中栖身，而大象、猴子和疣猪则以它的果实为食。
伊波利托还说，这些树具有巨大的文化意义。“它在非洲一直是神圣的树。无论你走到哪里：塞内加尔、马里、加纳——无论到哪里，只要有社区围绕着一棵猴面包树，那棵树就是神圣的，”她说。“某个人的高高高高高祖父母曾坐在那棵树下，它是那个地区人类历史的一部分。”
文特说，猴面包树根系较浅，因此不需要种得很深，而且这些根会较快重新长出。重新栽种后，这些树将用缆绳固定，并围上电围栏，以防大象破坏。
这些树据估计有200到300年树龄。文特说：“猴面包树很容易活到1000年，所以如果它们能活下来，前面还有几百年的寿命。”
一名据称对非法采挖和运输这些树木负有责任的园林公司老板已被立案调查。

items.title: 'It's a dream come true' – South African DJ celebrates featuring in GTA 6
items.summary: DJ lag, one of South Africa's best-known electronic music producers, is among several African stars to feature on Grand Theft Auto 6.
items.body:
Image source, Getty Images

Image caption,

DJ Lag is one of South Africa's best-known electronic music producers

ByWycliffe Muia

South African DJ Lag says it is a "dream come true" to have his music featured on Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6), the hugely popular video game released on Thursday.

DJ lag, one of South Africa's best-known electronic music producers, is among several African stars to feature, alongside Nigerian singers Burna Boy and Asake.

"I can't explain the feeling. I started playing the game last night and it's amazing," DJ Lag told the BBC's Newsday programme, adding that he had been playing GTA since he was about 10 years old and could hardly believe he was now part of the latest edition.

Many players have already had a chance to play the game following its worldwide launch.

The game, which lets players explore a fictional American city, features a dedicated African music radio station playing Afrobeats, amapiano and other sounds from across the continent.

The release of GTA 6 ends a 13-year wait for a new edition of the game.

Image source, Getty Images

Image caption,

GTA 6 is a satirical video series associated with crime and violence

Rockstar Games, the developer behind the franchise, has revealed details of the game's soundtrack and some in-game radio stations, but has yet to release a complete list of songs featured in the game.

Rockstar says AfroBank FM features everything from 20th Century African classics to contemporary amapiano and 3-step, giving the continent's music a prominent place in the latest edition.

Burna Boy co-hosts the station alongside British DJ and producer Palms Trax, while Asake's hit song Joha is among the tracks players can listen to as they drive around the game's virtual world.

DJ Lag, whose real name is Lwazi Asanda Gwala, is regarded as one of the pioneers of gqom, a genre of electronic dance music that emerged in the port city of Durban in the early 2010s.

He posted on Instagram: "God did."

Ghanaian highlife legends Pat Thomas and Ebo Taylor also feature, alongside South African artists Robot Boii and Kamo Mphela, bringing a mix of classic and contemporary African music to one of gaming's biggest franchises.

Rockstar has also announced a 34-track official soundtrack album, released in partnership with Atlantic Records, featuring an original Burna Boy song titled Bigger.

For African fans, the inclusion of familiar music adds another dimension to the experience, allowing players to hear some of the continent's biggest sounds while exploring the American setting.

The series allows players to roam through sprawling fictional cities, drive vehicles and complete missions involving crime, police pursuits and other adventures.

The latest instalment takes players to Vice City, a fictional version of Miami, and the surrounding US state of Leonida, inspired by Florida.

Its story follows two criminals, Jason and Lucia, who become caught up in a wider conspiracy after a robbery goes wrong.

The launch has generated enormous excitement among gamers around the world.

Some fans downloaded it in advance so they could begin playing as soon as it became available, while others have booked leave from work.

The previous edition, GTA 5, was one of the best-selling video games of all time, selling more than 200 million copies worldwide.

The new release is expected to be another major commercial success, although it remains to be seen whether it will match its predecessor's extraordinary sales.

items.title: Crimea bridge has been attacked again, says Russian-installed governor
items.summary: Assessment of damage under way, days after two attacks that destroyed road section of key bridge across Kerch strait linking annexed peninsula to Russia Apec summit – latest updates The remaining Kerch rail bridge connecting Crimea to Russia was attacked overnight, leading to a halt in train service…
items.body:
A satellite image of the Crimea bridge taken on 16 November. The key bridge connecting the peninsula to Russia has been attacked for a third time. Photograph: Airbus DS 2026/AP

A satellite image of the Crimea bridge taken on 16 November. The key bridge connecting the peninsula to Russia has been attacked for a third time. Photograph: Airbus DS 2026/AP

Crimea bridge has been attacked again, says Russian-installed governor

Assessment of damage is underway, days after two attacks that destroyed road section of key bridge across Kerch strait linking annexed peninsula to Russia

A key bridge connecting annexed Crimea to Russia has been attacked again, a Russian-appointed regional governor has said, two days after Ukrainian strikes caused serious damage to it.

“Following a new attack on the Crimean Bridge, traffic has been temporarily halted. All relevant services are on site and at work. An assessment of the damage is under way,” Sergei Aksyonov, the Kremlin-appointed governor of Crimea, wrote on Telegram.

Wednesday’s ‌attack is third this week on the highly symbolic bridge that links Russia with Crimea, which ​it seized from Ukraine in 2014. A 227-metre section of the road spanning the Kerch strait was destroyed this week, but the rail corridor appears to be operable despite sustaining some damage.

‘They were keeping it for a rainy day’: Ukraine’s Kerch bridge attack is proof Kyiv still has cards to play

Read more

The strike comes just hours before an unprecedented meeting between Russian president Vladimir Putin and his Chinese and American counterparts, Xi Jinping and Donald Trump, in China. One source in Ukraine’s armed forces said this week’s attacks were designed to embarrass Putin on the world stage. “The bridge is a symbol of Putin’s rule. Destroying it sends a message to the other two great leaders that Putin is not as strong as he pretends,” the person said.

For Ukraine, the bridge is a hated symbol of Russian arrogance and colonial thinking. Ukraine has previously declared that the bridge across the Kerch strait, built eight years ago, is illegal. Kyiv had tried twice to blow it up – with a truck bomb in 2022, and a sea drone the following year.

Earlier, Ukraine critically damaged the road section of the bridge in what President Volodymyr Zelenskyy hailed as an “unprecedented” military operation. A span of the bridge’s road section collapsed, but the railway line was still standing.

在两次袭击摧毁了横跨刻赤海峡、连接被吞并半岛与俄罗斯的关键大桥的路面路段数日后，损坏评估正在进行
一名俄方任命的地区行政长官表示，连接被吞并的克里米亚与俄罗斯的一座关键大桥再次遇袭，距乌克兰打击造成严重损坏仅两天。
“克里米亚大桥再次遇袭后，交通已暂时中断。各相关服务部门已到场工作。正在评估损毁情况，”克里姆林宫任命的克里米亚长官谢尔盖·阿克肖诺夫在Telegram上写道。
周三的袭击是本周对该象征意义极强、连接俄罗斯与克里米亚的大桥的第三次打击。俄罗斯于 2014 年从乌克兰夺取了克里米亚。横跨刻赤海峡的一段 227 米公路本周被摧毁，但铁路通道尽管有所受损，似乎仍可通行。

对乌克兰来说，这座桥是俄罗斯傲慢和殖民思维的可恨象征。乌克兰此前已宣布，这座八年前建成、横跨刻赤海峡的大桥是非法的。基辅曾两次试图炸毁它——2022 年用卡车炸弹，次年用海上无人机。

items.title: Survivors of Uganda's deadly landslide seek justice at the UN
items.summary: Survivors reject relocation plans they say ignore their safety, land rights and livelihoods.
items.body:
Image source, Getty Images

Image caption,

Bududa, eastern Uganda, has suffered repeated deadly landslides, including disasters in 2010 and 2018 that killed more than 142 people.

ByOndiro Oganga and Swaibu Ibrahim, BBC Africa, Reporting fromKampala

Updated 21 minutes ago

Survivors of a 2019 landslide in eastern Uganda that killed more than 50 people have taken their fight for relocation and compensation to the United Nations.

The 48 complainants accuse the government of violating Uganda's constitution by failing to put effective disaster management measures in Bududa, a mountainous district prone to landslides.

Their case comes as heavy rains raise the risk of further landslides. They say the government relocation programme ignores their safety, land rights and livelihoods.

The UN Human Rights Committee is considering what is believed to be the first case seeking climate adaptation measures, one that could set a global precedent.

The landslide struck Bududa in 2019, killing more than 53 people, including 33 children. Years later, survivors say every spell of heavy rain brings back fears of another tragedy.

William Tsama, one of the claimants, lost four members of his family members.

"My quest should be a lesson," he said.

"Victims in such situations, ignored by governments, can take them to court to compel them to help their citizens."

Uganda introduced a resettlement plan for landslide-prone areas in 2011, but progress has been limited, with relatively few people relocated.

Last month, it launched a new resettlement programme offering affected households 18 million Ugandan shillings ($4,300) to help them move to safer areas.

But some survivors have questioned whether the amount is enough to cover the cost of relocating and rebuilding their lives.

Under the programme, families can choose between receiving two acres of land, valued at 8 million shillings ($1,900), plus 10 million shillings (about $2,400) towards building a house, or taking the equivalent land allowance in cash, alongside the same housing grant.

The scheme is expected to benefit 1,410 households identified as living in high-risk areas.

The government has now given residents of designated high-risk areas two months, from November to December, to leave or face forced eviction.

The threat extends beyond landslides. The complainants say changing rainfall patterns and declining soil fertility have also affected farming, leaving many families struggling to secure their livelihoods.

"I want to get a new good place for my people, so even if I die, they will be okay. I am an old man, but I am doing it for my children," Tsama said.

The survivors first launched legal action in 2020 in Uganda, and received support from Ugandan environmental organisation Greenwatch three years later.

They are seeking compensation for lost family members and livelihoods, as well as emergency measures, including accessible early-warning systems in high-risk areas.

Greenwatch Executive Director Samantha Atukunda Kakuru Mwesigwa said the case is about changing how governments prepare and respond to climate-related disasters.

"Justice for claimants is not just about winning in court. It is about forcing government policy to keep pace with a changing climate, and ensuring loss and damage is no longer an afterthought in disaster management," she said.

The threat of climate-related disasters extends across East Africa.

In Kenya, floods and landslides killed at least 181 people between March and May 2024, according to the Kenya Red Cross. In Rwanda, floods and landslides killed 135 people in May 2023.

The dangers are also being felt further afield. In October 2026, a flash flood swept through Nepal's Gorkha district after a landslide blocked a river, washing away homes and infrastructure, and killing over 1,500 people.

"Disasters like the one in Bududa are only getting worse because of climate change – and they are happening all around the world, as we've seen recently and tragically in Nepal," ClientEarth lawyer Vesselina Newman said.

She said poorer countries, which have contributed relatively little to global emissions, are bearing some of the heaviest consequences of climate change and need greater financial support.

"High income countries must provide financial assistance and ensure that sufficient money goes directly to countries like Uganda, so they can roll out life-saving adaptation measures," she said.

The complainants say relocation must involve more than move people out of danger.

They want the government to protect their livelihoods, respect their land rights, and take account of individual needs.

The case is now before the United Nations Human Rights Committee, which will ask the Ugandan government to respond within six months.

translation.title: 乌干达致命山体滑坡的幸存者向联合国寻求公正
translation.label: 机器翻译

blocks.alt: Young children carrying bags on their heads walk through muddy ground past a cream-coloured house with a blue door, with a forested valley visible in the background after a landslide.

blocks.text: 图片来源：Getty Images
图片说明，
乌干达东部的布杜达一再遭受致命山体滑坡，其中包括 2010 年和 2018 年造成逾 142 人死亡的灾难。
奥恩迪罗·奥甘加、斯瓦伊布·易卜拉欣，BBC 非洲，发自坎帕拉
更新于 21 分钟前
2019 年乌干达东部一场造成逾 50 人死亡的山体滑坡的幸存者，已将争取搬迁与赔偿的抗争提交至联合国。
这 48 名申诉人指控政府未能在易发滑坡的山区布杜达县落实有效的灾害管理措施，从而违反了乌干达宪法。
他们的诉讼正值暴雨加大再次发生滑坡的风险之际。他们表示，政府的搬迁计划无视他们的安全、土地权利和生计。
联合国人权事务委员会正在审议这起据信是首例寻求气候适应措施的案件，它可能开创一项全球先例。
这场滑坡于 2019 年袭击布杜达，造成逾 53 人死亡，其中有 33 名儿童。数年过后，幸存者说，每一次暴雨都会让他们再度担心悲剧重演。
申诉人之一威廉·察马失去了四名家人。
他说：“我的这番求索应当成为一课。”
“在这类情况下被政府忽视的受害者，可以把政府告上法庭，迫使它们帮助本国公民。”
乌干达在 2011 年推出了针对滑坡易发区的安置计划，但进展有限，搬迁人数相对较少。
上个月，该国启动了新的安置项目，向受影响家庭提供 1800 万乌干达先令（4300 美元），帮助他们迁往更安全的地区。
但一些幸存者质疑，这笔金额是否足以支付搬迁和重建生活的成本。
根据该项目，家庭可以选择获得两英亩土地（价值 800 万先令，约 1900 美元），外加 1000 万先令（约 2400 美元）用于建房；也可以选择领取等额的土地补贴现金，同时仍获得同样的住房补助。
该计划预计将惠及被认定居住在高风险地区的 1410 户家庭。
政府现已要求指定高风险区的居民在 11 月至 12 月的两个月内离开，否则将面临强制驱逐。
威胁并不仅限于滑坡。申诉人表示，降雨模式变化和土壤肥力下降也影响了耕作，使许多家庭难以维持生计。
察马说：“我想给家里的人找一块新的好地方，这样即使我死了，他们也能过得好。我是个老人，但这是为孩子们做的。”
这些幸存者于 2020 年先在乌干达提起诉讼，三年后获得了乌干达环保组织 Greenwatch 的支持。
他们寻求对失去的家人和生计作出赔偿，并要求采取应急措施，包括在高风险地区建立便于使用的预警系统。
Greenwatch 执行董事萨曼莎·阿图昆达·卡库鲁·姆韦西格瓦表示，此案关乎改变政府准备和应对气候相关灾害的方式。
她说：“对申诉人而言，正义不只是打赢官司。它是要迫使政府政策跟上气候变化的步伐，并确保损失和损害不再是灾害管理中事后才想到的事情。”
与气候相关的灾害威胁遍及整个东非。
在肯尼亚，据肯尼亚红十字会称，2024 年 3 月至 5 月的洪水和滑坡至少造成 181 人死亡。在卢旺达，2023 年 5 月的洪水和滑坡造成 135 人死亡。
更远的地方也能感受到这些危险。2026 年 10 月，尼泊尔廓尔喀县在山体滑坡堵塞河流后突发山洪，冲走房屋和基础设施，造成逾 1500 人死亡。
ClientEarth 律师韦塞莉娜·纽曼说：“布杜达这样的灾害只会因气候变化而愈发严重——而且正如我们最近在尼泊尔悲惨所见，它们正在世界各地发生。”
她说，对全球排放贡献相对较小的较贫穷国家，正在承受气候变化的部分最沉重后果，需要更多资金支持。
她说：“高收入国家必须提供资金援助，并确保有足够的资金直接流向乌干达这样的国家，以便它们能够推行拯救生命的适应措施。”
申诉人表示，搬迁不能只是把人转移出危险地带。
他们希望政府保护他们的生计，尊重他们的土地权利，并顾及个人需求。
该案现已提交联合国人权事务委员会，委员会将要求乌干达政府在六个月内作出回应。

Parts of Bangladesh were shut down Thursday as protests by supporters of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina sparked clashes, bomb blasts and arson attacks, with the ancestral home ⁠of former leader Muhammad Yunus set ablaze in the violence.

Hasina’s Awami League party had called for a ​week-long programme of protests and rallies to mobilise support ‌for Hasina’s planned return in December, culminating in a ‌nationwide lockdown on Thursday.

Hasina, who has lived in exile in neighbouring India since she fled Dhaka following violent ⁠protests demanding her resignation in August 2024, has requested a new passport and identity card to facilitate her return. Her supporters are protesting against the government’s rejection of that request.

Police said former interim leader Yunus’ ancestral home in Chattogram, about 300km (186 miles) south-east of Dhaka, ​was set on fire late on ‌Wednesday.

It is likely that flammable ‌substances were thrown into an unused ground-floor room, police told Reuters, adding that Yunus’ paternal family members, who live on the upper floors, are safe.

Reuters could not immediately reach the Yunus Centre thinktank that speaks on his behalf to seek comment. Yunus and his government, which led Bangladesh after Hasina’s ouster, have faced hostility from her supporters.

During the last 10 days of protests, police have reported dozens of crude bomb blasts and incidents of ‌vehicles being set afire in at least 28 districts, injuring several police officials and members of the public, media have said.

Late on Tuesday, an activist of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist party (BNP) was allegedly killed by unidentified people during a protest near Hasina’s home district of Gopalganj, police said.

On the same night, a crude bomb exploded outside the Dhaka residence of cultural affairs minister Nitai Roy Chowdhury, and the house of a BNP lawmaker and shops ‌belonging to BNP supporters in Gopalganj were set on fire, police added.

On Wednesday morning, a bus company helper was burnt to death in the southern district of Pirojpur after two buses ​were set on fire, authorities said.

Tuesday marks a year since Hasina was ​sentenced to death by a local court that found her guilty of ordering a deadly crackdown on a student-led uprising against her in 2024. She has lived in exile in neighbouring India since fleeing Dhaka.

On Thursday, authorities detained former education minister Nurul Islam Nahid, who faces charges ⁠over several killings during the 2024 protests, from his house in Dhaka, police told Reuters.

At ​least 37 branches and offices of ​Grameen Bank, set up by Yunus, have been targeted in arson attacks or ​attempted fires since 10 November, ‌with 14 more ​attacked since midnight ​on Tuesday, the bank said.

政府拒绝哈西娜的护照申请后，人民联盟呼吁周四举行全国抗议
周四，孟加拉国部分地区因前总理谢赫·哈西娜支持者的抗议而陷入停摆，冲突、炸弹爆炸和纵火袭击相继发生，前领导人穆罕默德·尤努斯的祖宅也在暴力中被点燃。
哈西娜领导的人民联盟曾呼吁举行为期一周的抗议和集会，为她计划在 12 月回国动员支持，并以周四的全国封锁行动作为高潮。
哈西娜自 2024 年 8 月因要求她辞职的暴力抗议逃离达卡后，一直流亡邻国印度。她已申请新护照和身份证以便回国。她的支持者正在抗议政府拒绝这一申请。
一名发言人说，为遏制暴力，孟加拉国边境警卫队的 97 个排已分散部署到包括戈帕尔甘杰和法里德布尔在内的七个地区，这些地方被认为有许多哈西娜支持者。

警方对路透社表示，可能有人向一间闲置的一楼房间投掷了易燃物，并称住在楼上的尤努斯父系亲属均安然无恙。

路透社未能立即联系到代表尤努斯发声的智库尤努斯中心置评。尤努斯及其在哈西娜下台后领导孟加拉国的政府，一直面临她的支持者的敌意。
媒体称，警方通报，在过去 10 天的抗议中，至少 28 个地区发生数十起土制炸弹爆炸和车辆被纵火事件，数名警察和民众受伤。
警方说，周二晚间，执政党孟加拉国民族主义党（BNP）的一名活动人士在哈西娜家乡戈帕尔甘杰附近的抗议中据称被身份不明者杀害。
警方还说，同一晚，文化事务部长尼泰·罗伊·乔杜里位于达卡的住所外发生土制炸弹爆炸，戈帕尔甘杰一名 BNP 议员的住宅以及 BNP 支持者的商铺也遭纵火。
当局称，周三上午，南部皮罗杰布尔区有两辆巴士被人纵火，一名巴士公司帮工被烧死。

该银行表示，自 11 月 10 日以来，尤努斯创办的格莱珉银行至少有 37 家分行和办事处遭到纵火袭击或未遂纵火，另有 14 家自周二午夜起遇袭。

人民联盟领导人大多藏身隐匿，记者未能联系到他们置评。

items.body:
An inquest into the death of 47-year-old Aboriginal woman Tammy Michelle Shipley in Silverwater women’s correctional in 2022 has found it was the result of systemic failures. Photograph: Aboriginal Legal Service

An inquest into the death of 47-year-old Aboriginal woman Tammy Michelle Shipley in Silverwater women’s correctional in 2022 has found it was the result of systemic failures. Photograph: Aboriginal Legal Service

Tammy Shipley was supposed to be monitored in prison. Instead she died after drinking 20L of water

If the Aboriginal woman had been checked at regular intervals as required, her ‘excess consumption of water’ would have been prevented, inquest finds

Warning: This article contains images of and references to Indigenous Australians who have died

• Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The death of an Aboriginal woman who collapsed after drinking at least 20 litres of water in a New South Wales prison cell was preventable and the result of systemic failures, a coroner has found.

Tammy Michelle Shipley, 47, died at Silverwater women’s correctional centre on 20 December 2022.

State coroner Teresa O’Sullivan ruled on Thursday that her death was caused by low blood sodium levels resulting from excessive water consumption and complications of schizoaffective disorder.

“I’m confident in finding that Tammy’s death was preventable,” O’Sullivan said.

The mother-of-five had been taken into custody on remand 11 days earlier, after being charged with shoplifting offences, but didn’t disclose her mental health issues to police. Police also didn’t double-check her answers about her health, despite the fact she had attended a police station two weeks earlier and told them she heard her neighbour talking in her head.

O’Sullivan found there had been a missed opportunity to recognise the mental health issues that were present, and to potentially divert Shipley away from the criminal justice system.

Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email

When she appeared in a local court over the shoplifting charges the next day, the magistrate was not told she had been refused bail on other charges, so made orders they thought would secure her release.

“There was a clear systems failure,” O’Sullivan found.

Shipley should have been continually monitored – both physically and electronically – after twice attempting self-harm in custody.

It was a serious failure that this had not been done, O’Sullivan said.

“If observations had been carried out at the intervals required, it was likely that Tammy’s excess consumption of water would have been … prevented,” she said.

She deemed it unsatisfactory that Shipley had not been seen by a psychiatrist or mental health nurse at any point during the 11 days before her death.

She added that Shipley should have received medical care from the time she started vomiting, after 10am on the day of her death. Instead, she said, Shipley experienced seizures shortly before noon and was seen lying face down on the floor of her cell around an hour later.

A period of 23 minutes lapsed between when she was first seen lying on the ground and the commencement of resuscitation attempts, which the coroner found was unacceptable.

One corrective services officer had hastily closed the door to her cell after smelling faeces in the room earlier in the day.

“It was completely inappropriate that Tammy, who was known to be suffering a mental health condition, was left in that condition in her cell,” O’Sullivan said.

O’Sullivan made 10 recommendations to NSW police, Corrective Services NSW and Justice Health, including a review of the “austere and depressing” unit in which Shipley was held, which was intended to be a therapeutic space but left the coroner gravely concerned.

after newsletter promotion

She also recommended regular monitoring of footage inside the jail and improved maintenance and cross-checking of records related to mental health conditions.

The coroner acknowledged the jail had already made changes after Shipley’s death.

Outside the court, Shipley’s mother, Vicki, said she hoped the findings would force the system to assess how people are treated.

“I honestly thought that at this stage of our country’s development, we have moved past how convicts were treated,” she said.

“The system – every system – eventually caused trauma to my daughter, until eventually it killed her.”

Vickey Shipley urged the NSW government to quickly implement the recommendations.

“If they’re not made, there will be some other family standing here doing exactly the same thing that I am,” she said.

“All too often we hear the cry: ‘There’s not enough money.’

“How much is a life worth?”

blocks.text: 验尸官认定，一名原住民女性在新南威尔士州监狱牢房中饮用至少 20 升水后倒地死亡，此事本可避免，是系统性失误的结果。
47 岁的塔米·米歇尔·希普利于 2022 年 12 月 20 日在锡尔弗沃特女子矫正中心去世。
州验尸官特蕾莎·奥沙利文周四裁定，她的死亡是由过量饮水导致的血钠过低，以及分裂情感性障碍的并发症引起的。
奥沙利文说：“我有把握认定，塔米的死亡本可避免。”
这名五个孩子的母亲在 11 天前因商店盗窃指控被还押拘留，但没有向警方披露自己的精神健康问题。警方也没有复核她关于健康状况的回答，尽管两周前她曾到过警察局，并告诉他们自己听见邻居在脑子里说话。
奥沙利文认定，当时本有机会识别已存在的精神健康问题，并可能将希普利从刑事司法系统中分流出去，但这个机会被错过了。
订阅 Breaking News Australia 邮件
第二天她因商店盗窃指控出现在地方法庭时，治安法官并未得知她已因其他指控被拒绝保释，因此作出了他们以为能让她获释的命令。
奥沙利文认定：“这是明显的系统性失误。”
希普利在押期间曾两次试图自我伤害，此后本应持续接受身体和电子监控。
奥沙利文说，这件事没有做，是严重的失职。
她说：“如果按规定的间隔进行观察，塔米过量饮水的情况很可能本可……避免。”
她认为，希普利在去世前 11 天里一直未见过精神科医生或心理健康护士，这一点不能令人满意。
她还说，希普利从去世当天上午 10 点后开始呕吐起，就应得到医疗救治。但她表示，希普利在临近中午时出现癫痫发作，大约一小时后被人看见俯卧在牢房地板上。
从她首次被看见躺在地上，到开始抢救，中间过了 23 分钟，验尸官认为这令人无法接受。
当天早些时候，一名惩教人员闻到牢房里有粪便气味后，匆忙关上了她的房门。
奥沙利文说：“明知塔米患有精神疾病，却让她在牢房里处于那种状况，这完全不恰当。”
奥沙利文向新南威尔士州警方、新南威尔士州惩教署和 Justice Health 提出了 10 项建议，包括审查关押希普利的那处“肃杀压抑”的单元——那里本应是治疗空间，却让验尸官深感忧虑。
跳过新闻通讯推广
新闻通讯推广之后
她还建议定期查看监狱内部监控录像，并改进与精神健康状况有关的记录维护和交叉核对。
验尸官承认，监狱在希普利死后已经作出了改变。
庭外，希普利的母亲维基说，她希望这些调查结论能迫使这个系统重新审视人们是如何被对待的。

items.body:

The Markley Lowell datacentre in Lowell, Massachusetts. The US is expected to rely on gas to provide about 60% of the electricity for its datacentres by 2030. Photograph: Lauren Owens Lambert/AFP/Getty Images

Datacentres to create 70% more carbon emissions by 2030, IEA report warns

Global energy watchdog forecasts huge rise as US and China turn to fossil fuels to power AI growth agendas

The world’s datacentres will create 70% more carbon emissions within the next four years as the US and China turn to fossil fuels to power their AI growth agendas, according to the world’s energy watchdog.

The International Energy Agency (IEA) warned that datacentres will consume twice as much electricity by 2030 compared with today, with the global expansion of artificial intelligence accounting for three-quarters of this growth.

The Paris-based agency found that the breakneck pace of the industry’s growth means that within four years AI datacentres will consume an extra 350 terrawatt-hours of electricity every year, or more than the annual electricity consumption of Great Britain.

Its influential annual report warned that the world’s energy future was less certain after the impact of the Middle East war, which it has described as the greatest energy market disruption in history.

“I don’t see any credible pathway for the energy world to return to the way it was before,” said the IEA’s executive director Fatih Birol.

Instead, it will be reshaped by the policy decisions governments make after the crisis to meet the increasing demand for energy to power a growing global population, the rising need for air-conditioning and a booming AI economy, the IEA said.

A datacentre under construction at the Google Storey County campus in Sparks, Nevada, US. Photograph: Daniel Cole/Reuters

Datacentre developers have emerged as the world’s biggest corporate buyers of renewable energy to help fuel their servers which have a connection to local power grids. Despite this, the report showed that the appetite for fossil fuels is expected to grow even faster, particularly in the US and China.

By the end of the decade, around half of the electricity needed to power China’s AI datacentres will come from coal power plants, according to the IEA. The rest will come from renewable energy, with smaller amounts from nuclear reactors and very little from gas plants.

In contrast, the US is expected to rely on gas to provide about 60% of the electricity for its datacentres by 2030. There were plans for about 180GW of new gas-fired power plants linked to US datacentres in August this year, the agency said. That is almost as much new gas capacity as the total now installed across the European Union.

As a result of the growth in fossil fuel generation for datacentres, emissions associated with this sector were on track to rise by 70% by 2030, the IEA said.

The appetite for gas power among US datacentre developers is more than 16 times higher than in Canada, where the IEA identified plans for 11GW of gas generation to power their servers. In the rest of the world, AI developers have put forward plans for new gas plants with a combined capacity of just 4GW, the agency said.

This is because renewable energy is expected to play a greater role in supplying datacentres outside the US and China. In the EU, the IEA expects datacentres to rely on renewables for about 70% of their electricity by 2030 – followed by nuclear power, gas generation, and a very small amount of coal power.

Workers at TikTok’s datacentre in Hamar, Norway. Photograph: Victoria Klesty/Reuters

The agency based its forecasts for the notoriously opaque industry on data showing the annual global shipment of AI servers, which have climbed eighteen-fold since 2020. It also used space-based imagery to track the buildout of 93 large “AI factories” around the world.

Its analysis suggests that the world’s datacentre capacity has climbed tenfold in the last 24 months to 17GW. By the time the AI factories were completed, their combined capacity was likely to be about 50GW, the IEA said.

The world’s existing stock of datacentres, including those with AI-optimised servers, now stands at 120GW, with 80% of this capacity in China, the US and the EU. A further 120GW will be built by the end of the decade under the IEA scenario often considered its central base case, of which three-quarters will be AI datacentres.

blocks.text: 马萨诸塞州洛厄尔的 Markley Lowell 数据中心。预计到 2030 年，美国数据中心约 60% 的电力将来自天然气。照片：Lauren Owens Lambert/AFP/Getty Images
马萨诸塞州洛厄尔的 Markley Lowell 数据中心。预计到 2030 年，美国数据中心约 60% 的电力将来自天然气。照片：Lauren Owens Lambert/AFP/Getty Images
IEA 报告警告：到 2030 年，数据中心碳排放将增加 70%
全球能源监管机构预测将大幅上升，因美国和中国转向化石燃料以支撑人工智能增长计划
全球能源监管机构称，由于美国和中国转向化石燃料以支撑其人工智能增长计划，未来四年全球数据中心的碳排放将增加 70%。
国际能源署（IEA）警告称，到 2030 年，数据中心用电量将比今天增加一倍，其中全球人工智能扩张将占这一增长的四分之三。
这家总部位于巴黎的机构发现，该行业的飞速扩张意味着，四年内人工智能数据中心每年将额外消耗 350 太瓦时电力，超过英国一年的用电量。
这份有影响力的年度报告警告称，在中东战争冲击之后，世界能源前景更加不确定；该机构将这场战争称为历史上最严重的能源市场动荡。
“我看不到能源世界有任何可信的路径能回到从前的样子，”IEA 执行董事法提赫·比罗尔说。
IEA 表示，相反，它将由各国政府在危机后为满足不断增长的能源需求所做的政策决定所重塑，这些需求来自全球人口增长、空调需求上升以及蓬勃发展的人工智能经济。

blocks.alt: A datacentre under construction at the Google Storey County campus in Sparks, Nevada, US.

blocks.text: 美国内华达州斯帕克斯，Google 斯托里县园区内一座在建的数据中心。照片：Daniel Cole/Reuters
数据中心开发商已成为全球最大的企业可再生能源买家，为其接入当地电网的服务器供电。尽管如此，报告显示，对化石燃料的需求预计将增长得更快，尤其是在美国和中国。
据 IEA 称，到本十年末，中国人工智能数据中心所需电力约有一半将来自燃煤电厂。其余将来自可再生能源，核电占较小比例，天然气电厂则极少。
相比之下，预计到 2030 年，美国数据中心约 60% 的电力将来自天然气。该机构表示，截至今年 8 月，与美国数据中心相关的新建燃气电厂计划约有 180GW。这几乎相当于欧盟目前已装机的天然气发电总容量。
IEA 表示，由于数据中心化石燃料发电增加，该行业相关排放有望在 2030 年前上升 70%。
美国数据中心开发商对天然气发电的需求，是加拿大的 16 倍以上；IEA 在加拿大发现了 11GW 用于为服务器供电的天然气发电计划。该机构表示，在世界其他地区，人工智能开发商提出的新建天然气电厂合计装机仅 4GW。
这是因为预计可再生能源将在美国和中国以外的地区，在向数据中心供电方面发挥更大作用。IEA 预计，到 2030 年，欧盟数据中心约 70% 的电力将来自可再生能源，其次是核电、天然气发电，煤炭发电则非常少。

blocks.alt: Workers at TikTok’s datacentre in Hamar, Norway, finish construction of a huge steel building with exterior spiral staircases.

blocks.text: 挪威哈马尔 TikTok 数据中心的工作人员。照片：Victoria Klesty/Reuters
该机构对这一向来不透明的行业所做预测，基于全球人工智能服务器年出货量数据——自 2020 年以来已增长 18 倍。它还利用卫星影像追踪全球 93 座大型“人工智能工厂”的建设。
其分析表明，全球数据中心容量在过去 24 个月里增长了十倍，达到 17GW。IEA 表示，等到这些人工智能工厂建成，合计容量可能约为 50GW。
全球现有数据中心（包括配备人工智能优化服务器的设施）装机现为 120GW，其中 80% 在中国、美国和欧盟。按 IEA 通常被视为核心基准的情景，到本十年末还将再建 120GW，其中四分之三将是人工智能数据中心。

items.title: This is a remarkable diplomatic moment for China's Xi - but it comes with pitfalls
items.summary: The meeting comes with challenges as there are things Xi does not appear keen to discuss with Putin and Trump.
items.body:
Image source, Getty Images

Image caption,

Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping are meeting for a historic trilateral summit

ByLaura Bicker

China correspondent , Reporting fromShenzhen

Xi Jinping will believe he has achieved something no other world leader could in securing a historic summit with Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump in Shenzhen.

For decades, Washington and its western allies shaped the world order.

Yet it is China that has orchestrated the remarkable diplomatic spectacle of three of the world's most powerful protagonists sitting around the table.

And surrounding it all is the futuristic display that is Shenzhen, with driverless cars cruising past as drones fly overhead and robots - literally - dance in the streets.

Ostensibly, this is an economic summit for Asia Pacific leaders. But for Xi, it is also a demonstration of China's grip on the global economy and world politics.

His country is no longer just reacting to decisions made in Washington, London or Brussels - instead Beijing is at the heart of conversations which are reshaping the international order.

But this meeting is not without its pitfalls for Xi as there are many things he does not appear keen to discuss with Putin and Trump.

• Follow live updates: Trump, Xi and Putin hold historic meeting on Apec sidelines

Ukraine, the balancing act

First, China is not keen for the war in Ukraine, now well into its fourth year, to be on the agenda.

This is a delicate balancing act for Xi who is aware his relationship with Putin may damage China's connections in Europe. The EU is a key market, especially now when the Chinese economy is heavily relying on exports.

However Xi also doesn't want the war to end in a way that will destabilise Russia, a key ally and neighbour.

Beijing is still trying to maintain that it is neutral in this war and has repeatedly called for negotiations and a political settlement while avoiding condemnation of Russia's full-scale invasion.

Image source, Getty Images

Image caption,

Russia's invasion of Ukraine, now into its fourth year, has claimed hundreds of thousands of lives

The US, especially under the previous Biden administration, and Europe have accused China of sending Russia components that it could use in its war in Ukraine, while also propping up the country's economy by buying oil and gas.

Xi wants to keep Putin close, but not too close because he also doesn't want Russia's problems to become China's problems.

China's growing nuclear arsenal

Donald Trump has already made it clear he wants the three leaders to discuss limiting the world's supply of nuclear weapons.

The US and Russia possess the world's largest stockpile of nuclear warheads. But China is rapidly expanding its own arsenal, which is raising alarm bells in Washington.

The last major US-Russian arms control treaty, known as New START, expired in February this year, triggering fears of an arms race. The agreement had set a cap to control the number of nuclear weapons in US and Russia's arsenal.

Trump would like China to be included in any new agreement, but Beijing has pushed back.

Xi's argument will be that his arsenal is considerably smaller than what Washington and Moscow own, and, therefore, it would be unfair for Beijing to be bound by their limits. China also believes it should have the freedom to develop its own nuclear capabilities.

Image source, Getty Images

Image caption,

China unveiled intercontinental nuclear missiles at a military parade in 2025

This subject could complicate Xi's bid for China to be recognised as a leader on the world stage - because the US could argue that the status includes being a responsible nuclear power.

Will everyone stick to the script?

Xi will want to control the optics of this meeting, from start to finish.

Chinese officials like to nail down agendas with talking points and produce carefully choreographed speeches.

But in this unprecedented summit, Xi will have to live with two very unpredictable leaders.

Both Trump and Putin have their own agendas and the US President has already threatened to go off script.

There is a risk that they both dominate the meeting and Xi ends up looking like a host, rather than the architect of a major diplomatic moment.

Of course, Xi may be ready for this. It may even play into his hands.

The Chinese leader has been trying to portray himself as a stable global leader - at this summit he will be flanked by two men embroiled in wars they cannot seem to end.

So any unscripted moment could serve to highlight his preferred role as senior statesman.

Xi's problems at home

For all the attention, this meeting of three men with vastly different agendas is unlikely to yield any significant outcomes.

But the power it projects is important for Xi as he heads towards next year's Communist Party Congress, where he is expected to secure a historic fourth term as leader of the party and country.

Image source, Getty Images

Image caption,

A job fair in Jiangsu province: China has been battling youth unemployment in a sluggish economy

He may hope to use this as propaganda at home, given the country is grappling with huge domestic challenges.

A country-wide property crisis has dented consumer confidence. Local governments are heavily in debt. Manufacturing has slowed and more of China's workforce has become dependent on flexible jobs with no pension or social security. One in five young people are thought to be struggling to find work. Frustration and anxiety about the future bubble up routinely.

Xi does not have to deal with elections, and the country has not seen major protests in decades. But he will be concerned about his popularity within the party elite as these problems - and the palpable frustrations they produce - grow.

At a time like this, a photo-op with Putin and Trump may offer him proof that his country's "century of humiliation" is over. China is no longer a rising power, he can argue - rather, it is increasingly shaping the rules of a new era.

blocks.text: 图片来源：Getty Images
图片说明，
唐纳德·特朗普、弗拉基米尔·普京与习近平正在举行历史性三边峰会
作者：劳拉·比克
中国记者，发自深圳
习近平会认为，能促成与弗拉基米尔·普京和唐纳德·特朗普在深圳举行历史性峰会，是其他世界领导人做不到的事。
几十年来，华盛顿及其西方盟友塑造了世界秩序。
然而，正是中国促成了世界最有权势的三位主角同坐一席这一罕见的外交场面。
而环绕这一切的，是深圳充满未来感的景象：无人驾驶汽车驶过，无人机在头顶飞行，机器人——字面意义上——在街上跳舞。
表面上，这是一场亚太领导人经济峰会。但对习近平而言，这也是在展示中国对全球经济和世界政治的掌控力。
他的国家不再只是对华盛顿、伦敦或布鲁塞尔作出的决定作出反应——相反，北京正处在重塑国际秩序的讨论中心。
但对习近平来说，这次会晤并非没有隐患，因为有许多议题他似乎并不想与普京和特朗普讨论。

blocks.text: 乌克兰，平衡术
首先，中国并不希望已进入第四个年头的乌克兰战争被列入议程。
对习近平来说，这是一场微妙的平衡：他清楚自己与普京的关系可能损害中国在欧洲的联系。欧盟是关键市场，尤其是在中国经济严重依赖出口的当下。
不过习近平也不希望这场战争以动摇俄罗斯这个重要盟友和邻国的方式结束。
北京仍试图维持自己在这场战争中保持中立的立场，并一再呼吁谈判和政治解决，同时避免谴责俄罗斯的全面入侵。

图片说明，
俄罗斯对乌克兰的入侵已进入第四个年头，造成数十万人死亡
美国——尤其是在此前的拜登政府时期——以及欧洲，指责中国向俄罗斯输送可用于乌克兰战争的零部件，同时通过购买石油和天然气支撑俄罗斯经济。
习近平希望与普京保持亲近，但又不能太近，因为他也不希望俄罗斯的问题变成中国的问题。
中国不断扩充的核武库
唐纳德·特朗普已明确表示，希望三位领导人讨论限制全球核武器数量。
美国和俄罗斯拥有全球最大的核弹头库存。但中国正在迅速扩充自身核武库，这让华盛顿感到警觉。
美俄之间上一项重大军控条约 New START 已于今年 2 月到期，引发了对军备竞赛的担忧。该协议曾设定上限，以控制美俄核武库的数量。
特朗普希望任何新协议都把中国纳入其中，但北京方面已表示反对。
习近平的论点将是，中国的核武库远小于华盛顿和莫斯科所拥有的规模，因此让北京受制于他们的限额是不公平的。中国还认为，自己应有发展核能力的自由。

blocks.text: 图片来源：Getty Images

中国曾在 2025 年的阅兵式上展示洲际核导弹
这个议题可能使习近平让中国被承认为世界舞台领导者的努力变得复杂——因为美国可能主张，这一地位也包括成为负责任的核国家。
所有人都会按剧本走吗？
习近平会希望从头到尾掌控这次会晤的对外观感。
中国官员习惯用口径敲定议程，并准备精心编排的讲话。
但在这次前所未有的峰会上，习近平将不得不与两位非常难以预测的领导人共处。
特朗普和普京各有自己的议程，而美国总统已扬言要偏离既定剧本。
存在一种风险：两人主导会晤，而习近平到头来更像东道主，而不是这一重大外交时刻的主导者。
当然，习近平或许已有准备。这甚至可能对他有利。
这位中国领导人一直试图把自己塑造成稳定的全球领袖——在这次峰会上，他两侧将是两名深陷似乎无法结束的战争的人。
因此，任何不按剧本走的瞬间，都可能凸显他希望扮演的资深政治家角色。
习近平的国内难题
尽管备受关注，这三位议程迥异的领导人会晤，不太可能产生任何重大成果。
但对习近平而言，它所投射的力量很重要，因为他正走向明年的共产党代表大会，预计将在会上获得作为党和国家领导人的历史性第四个任期。

江苏一场招聘会：在经济放缓的背景下，中国一直在应对青年失业问题
鉴于国内正面临巨大挑战，他或许希望把这次会晤用作对内宣传。
全国性的房地产危机打击了消费者信心。地方政府债务高企。制造业放缓，越来越多的中国劳动力依赖没有养老金或社会保障的灵活就业。据认为，五分之一的年轻人难以找到工作。对未来的沮丧和焦虑经常涌上表面。
习近平不必应对选举，这个国家几十年未见大规模抗议。但他会担心自己在党内精英中的人气，因为这些问题——以及它们带来的明显不满——正在加剧。
在这样的时刻，与普京和特朗普的合影，或许能为他提供「百年屈辱」已经结束的证明。他可以主张，中国不再只是崛起中的大国，而是日益在塑造一个新时代的规则。

Seven countries in Africa expressly exempt husbands from prosecution for marital rape, including Côte d’Ivoire, Ethiopia and South Sudan. Photograph: Frank Dejongh/Unicef

One in four women globally unable to refuse sex within marriage, says UN

Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds

One in four women around the world has no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.

In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament. In Latin America and the Caribbean, one in 10 women are not able to refuse sex, said the report by the UN Population Fund (UNFPA) published on Thursday.

Younger women and girls aged 15 to 19 had even less power to say no, compared with older women aged 45 to 49, according to analysis in the report of eight countries with comparable data (Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kazakhstan, Malawi, Mali, Nigeria, Tajikistan and Zambia). The findings align with research showing adolescent girls endure very high rates of intimate partner violence.

“These are really sad figures,” said Jean-Paul Murunga, a lawyer with the global human rights organisation Equality Now. “Especially given that the continent of Africa as a whole has adopted the Maputo protocol, which sets [binding legal standards for] equality between women and men. We still have a lot of work to do to ensure women and girls benefit from these commitments.”

The Maputo protocol, a landmark treaty adopted by the African Union in 2003, guarantees women’s rights and obliges states to protect women from violence. It affirms that marriage must be based on full consent and guarantees women’s right to health.

“The underlying principle is unambiguous: sexual intercourse without free and voluntary consent constitutes sexual violence, including within marriage,” said Murunga. “Marriage does not create perpetual or implied consent. A woman retains the right to decide whether, when and how she engages in sexual activity”.

He said that as a first step rape laws across the continent needed to change. According to Murunga’s 2024 report, rape within marriage is not criminalised in some African countries. Seven countries expressly exempt husbands from prosecution for marital rape, including Côte d’Ivoire, Ethiopia and South Sudan. Some countries, such as Tanzania and Eritrea, only criminalise marital rape when the couple do not live together.

In countries where child marriage is permitted and marital rape is not criminalised, children are left unprotected. A legal loophole is created for what, outside marriage, would be classed as rape, and young wives have few options when it comes to protecting themselves from sexual violence and exploitation. In Gabon, for example, when a man has married a child he abducted, he can only be prosecuted after the marriage is annulled.

Underpinning these laws is the mistaken belief that marital rape does not exist as a concept because, by marrying, wives are assumed to have permanently consented to sex with their husbands. In many areas, religion plays a key role in affirming these beliefs.

Alimatu Dimonekene, founder of A Girl At A Time, an organisation supporting adolescent girls in Sierra Leone, said a conversation around consent in marriage had yet to begin in Africa. “We’ve not even started the conversation [around marital rape],” she said. “Women will never call it rape; they make excuses for it or even blame themselves.”

She added: “In west Africa, sex is seen as an obligation in marriage. You must do whatever your husband demands.

“Once he has paid your bride price [a traditional marriage custom in which the bride’s family are paid money, livestock or goods by the groom], he owns you and you cannot reject his demands. Whatever he wants, he gets, including in terms of intimacy, finances and raising the children.”

blocks.text: 非洲有七个国家明确免除丈夫因婚内强奸被起诉，其中包括科特迪瓦、埃塞俄比亚和南苏丹。摄影：Frank Dejongh/Unicef
非洲有七个国家明确免除丈夫因婚内强奸被起诉，其中包括科特迪瓦、埃塞俄比亚和南苏丹。摄影：Frank Dejongh/Unicef
联合国称，全球每四名女性中就有一人在婚姻中无法拒绝性关系
联合国人口基金发现，西非和中非近一半女性无法拒绝同意发生性关系，女童受影响最严重
联合国一份报告显示，全球四分之一的女性在丈夫或伴侣要求发生性关系时没有同意权。
在西非和中非，几乎一半女性（45%）在自己的婚姻中无法说不；在东非和南部非洲以及阿拉伯国家，三分之一的女性（33%）面临同样困境。在拉丁美洲和加勒比地区，十分之一的女性无法拒绝性关系。这是联合国人口基金（UNFPA）周四发布的报告所指出的。
根据报告对八个有可比数据的国家（安哥拉、刚果民主共和国、哈萨克斯坦、马拉维、马里、尼日利亚、塔吉克斯坦和赞比亚）的分析，15至19岁的年轻女性和女童，比起45至49岁的年长女性，说“不”的能力更弱。这些发现与显示青春期女童承受极高亲密伴侣暴力比率的研究相符。
“这些数字真的令人难过，”全球人权组织 Equality Now 的律师 Jean-Paul Murunga 说。“尤其考虑到整个非洲大陆已经通过了《马普托议定书》，它为男女平等设定了（具有约束力的法律标准）。我们仍有许多工作要做，以确保妇女和女童从这些承诺中受益。”
《马普托议定书》是非洲联盟于2003年通过的里程碑式条约，保障妇女权利并要求各国保护妇女免受暴力。它申明婚姻必须以充分同意为基础，并保障妇女的健康权。
“基本原则是明确的：未经自由自愿同意的性行为构成性暴力，包括在婚姻之内，”Murunga 说。“婚姻并不产生永久或默示的同意。女性仍然有权决定自己是否、何时以及以何种方式发生性关系。”
他说，第一步需要改变整个非洲大陆的强奸法律。根据 Murunga 2024 年的报告，一些非洲国家并未将婚内强奸定为犯罪。包括科特迪瓦、埃塞俄比亚和南苏丹在内的七个国家明确免除丈夫因婚内强奸被起诉。一些国家，如坦桑尼亚和厄立特里亚，仅在夫妻不同居时才将婚内强奸定为犯罪。
在允许童婚且婚内强奸未被定罪的国家，儿童得不到保护。这会为在婚姻之外本应被定性为强奸的行为制造法律漏洞，年轻妻子在保护自己免受性暴力和剥削方面几乎没有选择。例如在加蓬，一名男子娶了他绑架的儿童后，只有在婚姻被宣告无效之后才能被起诉。
支撑这些法律的是一种错误观念：婚内强奸这一概念并不存在，因为一旦结婚，妻子就被假定已永久同意与丈夫发生性关系。在许多地区，宗教在强化这些观念方面起着关键作用。
塞拉利昂支持少女的组织 A Girl At A Time 创始人 Alimatu Dimonekene 表示，非洲围绕婚内同意的讨论尚未开始。“我们甚至还没开始这场（关于婚内强奸的）对话，”她说。“女性永远不会称之为强奸；她们会为此找借口，甚至责怪自己。”
她还说：“在西非，性被视为婚姻中的义务。丈夫要求什么，你就必须做什么。
“一旦他付了你的彩礼（一种传统婚俗，由新郎向新娘家庭支付金钱、牲畜或物品），他就拥有了你，你不能拒绝他的要求。他想要什么就能得到什么，包括亲密关系、财务以及子女抚养。”

items.title: Elon Musk says record $446m spending on US midterms was 'pretty foolish'
items.summary: The multi-billionaire also said he was "not Maga", distancing himself from the political movement linked to Trump.
items.body:
Image source, Getty Images

ByOsmond Chia

Business reporter

Elon Musk said on Wednesday that he felt "pretty foolish" about the record sum he spent on the US midterm elections, following sweeping Republican defeats.

The Tesla and SpaceX CEO was the campaign's top individual donor, giving $446m (£339m) to support President Donald Trump's party, particularly in Texas where many of Musk's firms are based.

Musk, who had backed Trump's second White House bid, also said he was "not Maga" - the Make America Great Again movement associated with the president.

Democrats won control of the Senate and House, while Texas, Ohio and other states swung away from Trump, who has faced pressure over the impact his policies have had on the cost of living.

Musk was speaking virtually at the New York Times DealBook Summit, an annual conference hosted in the city attended by major business and political leaders.

"I'm not Maga," Musk said, referring to the right-wing political movement.

He added: "I'm not sure what Maga means... if that means sort of blind adherence to a set of policies by the Republican Party, then I certainly don't have that."

Musk went on to say he did not see much for the money he had spent on the Republicans' campaign, though he added that it was likely that candidates would have fared worse without the spending.

One of the most striking midterms wins went to Democrat James Talarico, who beat Republican Ken Paxton for a US Senate seat in Texas.

According to BBC analysis, Musk had spent at least $45m in support of Paxton.

Texas is where key operations for Musk's car company Tesla and rocket and technology firm SpaceX are based.

Democrats have vowed greater scrutiny of tech companies, including over the roll out of controversial data centres.

blocks.text: 图片来源：Getty Images
作者：Osmond Chia
商业记者
埃隆·马斯克周三表示，在共和党遭遇全面败选后，他对自己在美国中期选举中创纪录的支出感到“相当愚蠢”。
这位 Tesla 和 SpaceX 首席执行官是此次竞选中最大的个人捐款人，捐出 4.46 亿美元（3.39 亿英镑）支持唐纳德·特朗普总统的政党，尤其是在马斯克多家公司所在的得克萨斯州。

民主党赢得了参议院和众议院的控制权，而得克萨斯州、俄亥俄州等州则偏离特朗普。特朗普因其政策对生活成本的影响而面临压力。

items.title: Van Gogh painting sells for record $190.4m after row over its Nazi history
items.summary: Châtaigniers en fleurs was painted in 1890 in the final two months of Vincent van Gogh's life.
items.body:
Image source, Getty Images

Image caption,

Sotheby's staff handle the "Châtaigniers en fleurs" painting by Vincent van Gogh at an auction preview in Hong Kong last month

BySareen Habeshian

Auction house Sotheby's has sold a painting by Vincent van Gogh for a record $190.4m (£144.8m).

The sale of Châtaigniers en fleurs ("Chestnut Trees in Blossom") shatters the renowned artist's previous auction record of $117.2 million set in 2022.

The historic sale in New York on Wednesday comes after an eleventh-hour agreement was reached to resolve a dispute regarding claims the art piece was previously sold under duress during the rise of the Nazis.

Châtaigniers en fleurs was painted in 1890 in the final two months of Van Gogh's life. It is considered one of the most important works of art from that period to remain in private hands, according to Sotheby's.

• Sotheby's auction of $180m Van Gogh challenged over claims it was 'sold under duress'Published4 days ago

It was not immediately clear who purchased the painting. The BBC has contacted Sotheby's for comment.

The oil painting, which was estimated to carry a value of $180m (£136m) prior to the sale, was put up for auction as part of a set called the Blaquier-Arrieta Collection.

Sotheby's announced in the hours before the auction that it had resolved a dispute between the Blaquier-Arrieta family and the heirs of the Fischer family - the prior German owners of the work - regarding the sale.

Representatives acting for heirs of the Fischer family had claimed the painting may have been sold under duress during the rise of the Nazis.

A lawyer for the family's heirs reportedly wrote to Sotheby's on their behalf, telling the auction house that the painting was sold in Amsterdam before World War Two because of financial losses the Fischer family's publishing company suffered under the Nazis. The BBC has contacted the lawyer for comment.

"In recognition of the painting's complex Nazi-era history and the suffering endured by the Fischer family during the Holocaust, the two families have reached a mutually satisfactory resolution and the work will be sold pursuant to their agreement," Sotheby's said on Wednesday.

Sotheby's website details the provenance of the oil painting and how it has researched the artwork changing hands since 1890.

It says Samuel Fischer - a famous German publisher - acquired it 1909 before it was passed down in his family after his death in 1934.

The painting was deposited with Paul Cassirer in Amsterdam in 1932 or 1933 before it went to Henriette and Marcel Kapferer in Paris in 1936, Sotheby's said.

Four other owners then had the painting.

The Blaquier family acquired it in 1975 and owned it for more than half a century before the latest sale, the auction house said.

图片说明，
苏富比工作人员上月在香港预展上整理文森特·梵高的画作《开花的栗树》（Châtaigniers en fleurs）
作者：Sareen Habeshian
拍卖行苏富比以创纪录的1.904亿美元（1.448亿英镑）拍出一幅文森特·梵高的画作。
《开花的栗树》（Châtaigniers en fleurs，Chestnut Trees in Blossom）的成交价打破了这位著名画家2022年创下的1.172亿美元拍卖纪录。
周三在纽约的这场历史性拍卖，是在最后时刻达成协议、解决该作品曾在纳粹崛起期间遭胁迫出售的争议之后举行的。
《Châtaigniers en fleurs》绘于1890年，正值梵高生命的最后两个月。苏富比表示，它被认为是该时期仍由私人持有的最重要作品之一。

items: 苏富比1.8亿美元梵高拍卖因“遭胁迫出售”指控受到质疑发布于4天前

blocks.text: 目前尚不清楚是谁买下了这幅画。英国广播公司已联系苏富比寻求置评。
这幅油画在拍卖前估值1.8亿美元（1.36亿英镑），作为布拉基耶-阿里埃塔收藏的一部分上拍。
苏富比在拍卖开始前数小时宣布，已解决布拉基耶-阿里埃塔家族与该作品先前德国所有者菲舍尔家族继承人之间关于此次出售的争议。
代表菲舍尔家族继承人的代理方曾主张，这幅画可能是在纳粹崛起期间遭胁迫出售的。
据报道，该家族继承人的律师代表他们致信苏富比，告知拍卖行这幅画在第二次世界大战前于阿姆斯特丹售出，原因是 Fischer 家族的出版公司在纳粹统治下遭受了财务损失。BBC 已联系该律师征求置评。
Sotheby's 周三表示：“考虑到这幅画在纳粹时期的复杂历史以及菲舍尔家族在大屠杀中遭受的苦难，两个家庭已达成双方满意的解决方案，该作品将根据他们的协议出售。”
苏富比网站详细介绍了这幅油画的来源，以及他们如何研究这件艺术品自1890年以来的易手情况。
据称，著名德国出版商塞缪尔·菲舍尔于1909年购得该物，1934年他去世后，这件物品便在其家族中代代相传。
苏富比表示，这幅画于1932年或1933年存放在阿姆斯特丹的保罗·卡西雷尔处，1936年到了巴黎的亨丽埃特与马塞尔·卡普费雷手中。
随后还有另外四位所有者持有过这幅画。
拍卖行表示，布拉基耶家族于1975年购得该画，持有了半个多世纪，直至此次出售。
