items.title: India's religious make-up - what a new Pew study says about Hindus and Muslims
items.summary: India will remain predominantly Hindu, though its Muslim population is projected to grow faster, according to a new survey.
items.body:
Image source, AFP via Getty Images

Image caption,

An Indian woman lights lamps on the occasion of Diwali, the Hindu festival of lights

India will remain overwhelmingly Hindu for decades to come, but its religious composition is projected to shift gradually.

A new study by the Pew Research Center, projecting the world's religious populations to 2070, estimates that Hindus will make up 76% of India's population by then, down from 79% in 2020, while the Muslim share will rise from 15% to 20%.

The shift is rooted largely in differences in age and fertility: Indian Muslims are younger than Hindus and, on average, have more children.

The Pew projections place India at the centre of a wider demographic shift across South Asia.

Pakistan is expected to overtake Indonesia as the country with the world's largest Muslim-majority population, with India moving into second place. Bangladesh, too, is projected to see substantial growth in its Muslim population.

The study projects the religious composition of the world over the next 50-year period, drawing on data from 201 countries and territories, covering virtually the entire global population.

Image source, Hindustan Times via Getty Images

Image caption,

Muslims offer prayer at the historic Jama Masjid in Delhi

It tracks seven religious groups between 2020 and 2070, assuming recent demographic trends continue. Using census and survey data, it establishes each group's size and age profile in 2020, and factors in differences in fertility and religious switching.

The findings place India at the heart of a changing global religious landscape. The country is expected to have the world's second-largest Muslim population by 2070, after Pakistan, with about 334 million Muslims. Pakistan itself will overtake Indonesia as the country with the largest Muslim population, with an estimated 461 million.

Yet the projections offer little support for the more dramatic narratives sometimes attached to India's changing religious composition.

If current demographic trends continue, the Hindu population in the country is expected to grow by 176 million between 2020 and 2070, the report says. It will continue to account for more than three-quarters of the country's population.

Despite a sharp fall in India's overall fertility, Muslim women still have more children, on average, than Hindu women. Pew attributes the shift primarily to demographic momentum.

Indian Muslims had a median age of 24 in 2020, compared with 29 for Hindus.

Between 2025 and 2030, Pew estimates Muslim women in India will have an average of 2.3 children, against 1.8 among Hindu women.

"We expect religious change in India to be driven almost entirely by long-standing demographic differences between Hindus and Muslims: Muslims are younger and have higher fertility rates," Stephanie Kramer of the Pew Research Center told the BBC.

Image source, Getty Images

Image caption,

Hindu devotees offer prayers on the banks of the Sabarmati river in India's Gujarat

"The fertility gap has narrowed considerably – from more than one child per woman in 1992 to about half a child in recent years and is likely to keep shrinking," she said.

"But Hindu fertility is already below the replacement level, while Muslim fertility is projected to remain above it for another two decades." (A replacement level is one at which new births are sufficient to maintain a stable population.)

The projections are hardly surprising, says KS James, an Indian demographer at Princeton University.

"The fertility gap between Muslims and Hindus is well established and it means Muslim population growth is likely to remain faster for the next few decades. But fertility is declining across all religious communities and the gap is expected to narrow further," he told the BBC.

"Ultimately, they will converge," he says, adding that the projections do not point to anything dramatically different in India's demographic trajectory.

Demographers push back against claims, often amplified by Hindu right-wing groups, that Muslims will eventually outnumber Hindus. There is no evidence of any significant religious conversion driving population change in India, they say, and the projections do not support such "alarmist scenarios".

Image source, Hindustan Times via Getty Images

Image caption,

Muslim children dressed in festive attire in India

The wider South Asian picture is equally revealing, according to the report.

Pakistan's Muslim population is projected to more than double to 461 million by 2070, overtaking Indonesia as the world's largest. India will rank second, with 334 million Muslims, while Bangladesh's Muslim population will rise to 218 million. India and Nepal, meanwhile, will remain the world's only Hindu-majority countries.

There appears to be a global story behind these regional shifts.

By 2035, Muslims are projected to overtake Christians as the world's largest religious group, according to the report. By 2070, their numbers are expected to reach 3.64 billion, up from 2.02 billion in 2020.

Christianity, meanwhile, will have just under three billion followers. Muslims will account for 36% of humanity, compared with 26% today.

But the most dramatic transformation may be taking place thousands of miles west of South Asia, in Africa.

Christianity's centre of gravity is moving steadily away from Europe and the Americas towards sub-Saharan Africa.

The report says that if recent trends continue, more than half of the world's Christians are expected to live there by 2070, compared with 31% in 2020. Pew forecasts that the Democratic Republic of Congo will overtake the United States as the country with the largest Christian population.

Image source, Hindustan Times via Getty Images)

Image caption,

With more than 1.4 billion people, India overtook China in 2023 in terms of population, according to the UN

The steepest decline is expected to occur in Europe. If current trends continue, by 2070 Europe will be home to 11% of the world's Christian population, down from 22% in 2020, the report says.

The US is projected to lose its Christian majority by 2065, although Christians will remain the country's largest religious group in 2070.

One reason for this changing religious landscape is the growing number of people identifying with no religion.

In UK and France, the "religiously unaffiliated" are projected to become the majority by 2070. South Korea is expected to follow suit.

Yet their share of the world's population is forecast to fall from 24% to 17%, largely because of a decline in China's population.

China accounts for about two-thirds of the world's religiously unaffiliated population. Its expected population decline will more than offset growth in secular populations elsewhere, the report says.

By 2070, there are other unexpected shifts.

The US is projected to become the world's fifth-largest Hindu population, with immigration driving much of its growth.

And Australia's unaffiliated population will overtake Christians as the country's largest group.

Buddhism, meanwhile, faces a demographic squeeze. Its population is expected to fall by more than half in China, Japan and South Korea, reflecting the ageing and shrinking populations of East Asia. Laos and Mongolia are projected to lose their Buddhist majorities.

Image source, AFP via Getty Images

Image caption,

Muslims offer Eid prayers in Pakistan

There are, of course, caveats. These are demographic projections, not predictions of everything that might happen. Pew assumes that recently observed patterns of fertility, migration and religious switching - or conversions - will continue.

"There are many events that could affect religious group populations (including wars, natural disasters, epidemics and changes in economic or social circumstances) that are not analysed here," the report admits.

India's baseline also required projecting the 2020 religious composition from the 2011 census, because the subsequent census had been delayed

Still, the broad direction is unmistakable.

South Asia will remain indispensable to the world's religious story, not just because of India's enormous Hindu population but because of the growing weight of its Muslim populations. Africa will increasingly shape Christianity's future, while Europe and parts of East Asia become more secular.

Clearly, by 2070, the world's religious landscape may look markedly different, shaped less by conversion than by the uneven arithmetic of births, deaths and migration.

巴基斯坦预计将超过印度尼西亚，成为全球穆斯林占多数人口最多的国家，印度升至第二。孟加拉国的穆斯林人口预计也将大幅增长。
该研究基于 201 个国家和地区的数据，覆盖几乎全球人口，对未来 50 年世界的宗教构成作出预测。

图片说明，
穆斯林在德里历史悠久的贾玛清真寺礼拜
它追踪2020年至2070年间七个宗教群体，假定近期人口趋势持续。它利用人口普查和调查数据，确定各群体在2020年的规模和年龄结构，并计入生育率和改宗方面的差异。
这些发现将印度置于全球宗教格局变化的核心。到 2070 年，该国预计将拥有世界第二大穆斯林人口，约 3.34 亿，仅次于巴基斯坦。巴基斯坦本身将超过印度尼西亚，成为穆斯林人口最多的国家，估计为 4.61 亿。
不过，这些预测很难支撑人们有时给印度宗教构成变化附加的那些更夸张的说法。
报告称，如果当前人口趋势持续，该国印度教徒人口预计在 2020 至 2070 年间将增加 1.76 亿，并将继续占全国人口的四分之三以上。
尽管印度总体生育率大幅下降，穆斯林女性平均生育的孩子仍多于印度教女性。皮尤将这一变化主要归因于人口惯性。
2020 年，印度穆斯林的年龄中位数为 24 岁，印度教徒为 29 岁。
皮尤估计，2025 至 2030 年，印度穆斯林女性平均会生育 2.3 个孩子，印度教女性为 1.8 个。
皮尤研究中心的斯蒂芬妮·克拉默对英国广播公司表示：“我们预计，印度的宗教变化几乎完全将由印度教徒与穆斯林之间长期存在的人口结构差异所驱动：穆斯林更年轻，生育率也更高。”

The ritual thanks the Sun god for sustaining life on Earth and seeks blessings for families' well-being. (Photo by Saurabh Sirohiya/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

blocks.text: 图片来源：Getty Images
图片说明，
印度教徒在印度古吉拉特邦萨巴尔马蒂河岸边祈福
「生育差距已大幅缩小——从 1992 年每位女性相差一个以上孩子，降到近年来约半个孩子，而且可能继续缩小，」她说。
「但印度教徒的生育率已经低于更替水平，而穆斯林的生育率预计还将在更替水平之上再维持二十年。」（更替水平是指新生儿数量足以维持人口稳定的水平。）
普林斯顿大学的印度人口学家 KS James 说，这些预测并不令人意外。
他告诉 BBC：“穆斯林与印度教徒之间的生育率差距是公认的，这意味着未来几十年穆斯林人口增长可能仍会更快。但所有宗教群体的生育率都在下降，这一差距预计还会进一步缩小。”
「最终他们会趋同，」他说，并补充这些预测并不表明印度的人口轨迹会出现任何戏剧性的不同。
人口学家反驳了常被印度教右翼团体放大的说法，即穆斯林最终将超过印度教徒。他们表示，没有证据表明印度的人口变化是由大规模宗教改宗驱动的，相关预测也不支持这类“危言耸听的情景”。

印度身着节日盛装的穆斯林儿童
报告称，更广泛的南亚图景同样说明问题。
巴基斯坦的穆斯林人口预计到 2070 年将增加一倍以上，达到 4.61 亿，超过印度尼西亚成为世界第一。印度将排第二，有 3.34 亿穆斯林，而孟加拉国的穆斯林人口将增至 2.18 亿。与此同时，印度和尼泊尔仍将是世界上仅有的印度教占多数的国家。
这些地区性变化背后，似乎有一个全球性的故事。
报告称，到 2035 年，穆斯林预计将超过基督徒，成为全球最大的宗教群体。到 2070 年，其人数预计将从 2020 年的 20.2 亿增至 36.4 亿。
与此同时，基督教信徒将略少于 30 亿。穆斯林将占人类的 36%，而目前为 26%。
但最剧烈的变化，可能正在南亚以西数千英里的非洲发生。
基督教的重心正逐步从欧洲和美洲转向撒哈拉以南非洲。
该报告称，如果近期趋势持续，到 2070 年，全球超过一半的基督徒预计将生活在那里，而 2020 年这一比例为 31%。皮尤（Pew）预测，刚果民主共和国将超过美国，成为拥有最多基督徒人口的国家。

联合国的数据显示，印度人口超过 14 亿，已于 2023 年在人口数量上超过中国

预计美国将在 2065 年失去基督徒占多数的地位，不过到 2070 年，基督徒仍将是该国最大的宗教群体。
宗教格局变化的一个原因，是自称无宗教信仰的人越来越多。
在英国和法国，「无宗教信仰者」预计将在 2070 年成为多数。韩国预计也会步其后尘。
不过，他们占世界人口的比重预计将从 24% 降至 17%，主要原因是中国人口减少。
报告称，全球无宗教信仰人口约三分之二在中国。中国预期中的人口下降，将超过其他地区世俗人口的增长。
到 2070 年，还会出现其他意想不到的变化。
预计美国将成为全球印度教徒人数第五多的国家，其增长主要来自移民。
而在澳大利亚，无宗教信仰者将超过基督徒，成为该国最大群体。
与此同时，佛教正面临人口挤压。其信众人数预计将在中国、日本和韩国减少一半以上，反映出东亚人口老龄化和萎缩。老挝和蒙古预计将失去佛教徒占多数的地位。

blocks.alt: Shia Muslims offer Eid al-Fitr prayers, which marks the end of the Islamic holy fasting month of Ramadan, in Skardu, Pakistan's Gilgit-Baltistan, on March 21, 2026.

blocks.text: 图片来源：AFP via Getty Images

巴基斯坦穆斯林进行开斋节礼拜
当然也有注意事项。这些是人口预测，不是对可能发生的一切的预言。皮尤假设近期观察到的生育、移民和宗教改宗——或者说皈依——模式将会持续。
报告承认：「还有许多可能影响各宗教群体人口的事件（包括战争、自然灾害、流行病以及经济或社会环境的变化）未在此分析。」

不过，大方向仍清晰可辨。
南亚仍将在世界宗教格局中不可或缺，不仅因为印度庞大的印度教人口，也因为其穆斯林人口的分量日益增加。非洲将越来越多地塑造基督教的未来，而欧洲和东亚部分地区则将更加世俗化。
显然，到 2070 年，世界的宗教格局可能大不相同，其塑造因素与其说是皈依，不如说是出生、死亡和移民的不均衡算术。

items.body:
Why has Waymo pulled all its driverless cars from US freeways?

Why has Waymo pulled all its driverless cars from US freeways?

Waymo has temporarily suspended driverless rides on US freeways after California banned the service over safety concerns.

California's Department of Motor Vehicles said a series of traffic incidents, including robotaxis entering active construction zones, posed an imminent risk to public safety. Waymo has now restricted freeway operations in all other US markets while it reviews the performance of its vehicles.

Waymo currently operates in 15 US cities, though only offered driverless freeway rides in a handful of cities, including San Francisco and Los Angeles.

items.title: The seven Anthropic founders who are about to become multi-billionaires
items.summary: The AI company behind Claude is about to sell its shares on the US stock market - making its founders very rich.
items.body:
Image source, David Paul Morris/Bloomberg via Getty Images

Image caption,

Brother and sister Dario and Daniela Amodei

In the space of just five years, Anthropic has gone from unknown start-up to tech giant, worth more than a trillion dollars.

The company behind the AI platform Claude was formed by seven people who left rival OpenAI in 2021 and, in a matter of hours, will become multi-billionaires - on paper at least.

Anthropic is floating the business on the US stock exchange and will sell its shares at between $70 - $78 each.

If they go for the highest price, the founders' shareholdings will be worth at least $18.5bn each.

So, who are these people, all in their thirties and forties, who are about to become incredibly wealthy?

Dario Amodei

Image source, Finn Gomez/Getty Images

In 2020, Dario Amodei was working for OpenAI, the firm that brought generative artificial intelligence to a mainstream audience, when it launched Chat-GPT.

He decided he wanted to do things his own way, and left, taking his sister Daniela, and five colleagues with him.

Amodei grew up in San Francisco, impressing school friends not just with his academic prowess but also his speed on the running track, and his preoccupation with philosophical and technological questions including the potential of machines to gain consciousness and human longevity.

Initially he studied physics at Princeton and Stanford. But following his father's death from hepatitis C, he switched to biology and biomedical sciences.

Amodei did stints at the Chinese tech giant Baidu and Google before joining OpenAI.

But he began to worry that some people within the company were putting profit before safety, prompting the decision to jump ship.

Now 43, he is Anthropic's chief executive, and the person who, in his sister's words, makes the company "ambitious".

• Listen: Dario Amodei BBC Sounds profile

Daniela Amodei

Image source, Jason Henry/Bloomberg via Getty Images

Dario and Daniela Amodei, were close growing up and later shared a flat together in San Francisco with other friends. She followed him into OpenAI and joined him when he left to found Anthropic.

She and her brother have always genuinely liked each other, she says, but the only thing she ever did first, was when he followed her in becoming vegetarian.

Amodei studied English Literature at the University of California Santa Cruz, going on to work for Democrat representative Matt Cartwright.

She has also worked at financial services platform Stripe, where she was head of risk operations.

The 39-year-old is president of Anthropic, manages the executive team, and leads the firm's research, engineering, product, governance and commercial work.

Tom Brown

Image source, Cornell Watson/Bloomberg via Getty Images

Tom Brown, now 39, followed the Amodei siblings when they left to found their new venture.

He led GPT-3 engineering at OpenAI, and prior to that was at Google on its DeepMind project.

Brown established his entrepreneurial credentials co-founding an app called "Grouper" that helps set up drinks between groups of friends.

He has supported US President Donald Trump's stance on datacentres, arguing that they are "an enormous source of prosperity".

Now as chief compute officer at Anthropic he is responsible for how the company secures and uses its computing resources.

Jack Clark

Image source, Peerapon Boonyakiat/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images

Jack Clark, is another arts graduate among the original start-up's founding members and the only one who is not from North America.

Originally from Brighton in the UK, he studied English Literature and Creative Writing at the University of East Anglia and became a technology journalist, writing for publications including ZDNet UK, The Register, and Bloomberg.

He was caught up in the excitement of artificial intelligence and joined OpenAI, where he worked initially in communications, later becoming its policy director.

Now, 37, Clark is head of public benefit at Anthropic. He also leads the Anthropic Institute, an AI think tank.

Jared Kaplan

Image source, Chris J. Ratcliffe/Bloomberg via Getty Images

Jared Kaplan, 42, is chief science officer at Anthropic, and heads its technical research. He is also an associate professor at Johns Hopkins University in Baltimore.

He holds a PhD in physics from Harvard University.

His work on scaling laws - which describe mathematical patterns that show that bigger AI models trained on more data tend to be more consistent - has helped provide AI firms with a framework for predicting AI behaviour, according to Anthropic.

Chris Olah

Image source, Alberto PIZZOLI / AFP via Getty Images

Chris Olah is described as "interpretability research lead" primarily focused on how AI models work with each other.

But according to the New York Times, Olah has spent much of the last year convening meetings with faith leaders from across the religious spectrum.

Described by the newspaper as "boyish" but with "the zeal of an evangelist" the 34-year-old is reportedly exploring the relationship between morality and AI.

He previously led interoperability research at OpenAI, and prior to that was a research scientist at Google Brain.

The Canadian left Toronto University early, but later secured a Thiel Fellowship of $100,000, which is a scholarship to help gifted people move into research without a degree.

Sam McCandlish

Image source, Anthropic

Sam McCandlish, 36, takes less of a public-facing role than the other founders, but like them will own around 1.6% of the company after its shares go on sale. As a result he too will see his stake crystallise into a hugely valuable asset.

McCandlish is Anthropic's chief architect, and helps shape and implement the company's policy designed to mitigate the risks of AI. Prior to this he worked on safety at OpenAI.

He has a physics PhD from Stanford, and maths and physics degree from Brandeis University outside Boston.

但他开始担心公司内部有些人把利润置于安全之上，于是决定跳槽离开。
现年 43 岁的他是 Anthropic 的首席执行官，用他妹妹的话说，正是他让这家公司「胸怀大志」。

她说，她和哥哥一直真心喜欢对方，但她唯一先做的一件事，是他跟着她一起吃素。
阿莫代曾在加州大学圣克鲁兹分校学习英国文学，随后为民主党众议员马特·卡特赖特工作。
她还曾在金融服务平台 Stripe 工作，担任风险运营负责人。
这位39岁的人士是 Anthropic 的总裁，负责管理高管团队，并领导公司的研究、工程、产品、治理和商务工作。

他曾在 OpenAI 负责 GPT-3 工程，此前在 Google 参与 DeepMind 项目。
布朗通过联合创办帮助朋友圈之间约酒的应用「Grouper」，奠定了自己的创业资历。
他支持美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在数据中心问题上的立场，称它们是“巨大的繁荣来源”。
如今作为 Anthropic 的首席算力官，他负责公司如何保障和使用计算资源。

Jack Clark 是这家初创公司原始创始成员中又一位文科毕业生，也是其中唯一不是来自北美的人。
他原先来自英国布莱顿，在东英吉利大学学习英语文学和创意写作，后来成为科技记者，曾为 ZDNet UK、《The Register》和 Bloomberg 等媒体撰稿。
他被人工智能的热潮吸引，加入了 OpenAI，起初从事传播工作，后来成为其政策主管。
现年 37 岁的克拉克是 Anthropic 的公益负责人。他还领导人工智能智库 Anthropic Institute。

blocks.alt: Jared Kaplan wears a biege teeshirt and sits on a stage talking into a small headset microphone

42岁的贾里德·卡普兰是 Anthropic 的首席科学家，负责其技术研究。他也是巴尔的摩约翰斯·霍普金斯大学的副教授。
他拥有哈佛大学物理学博士学位。
据 Anthropic 称，他在扩展定律（scaling laws）方面的研究——这些定律描述了更大、用更多数据训练的人工智能模型往往更稳定的数学规律——帮助为人工智能公司提供了预测人工智能行为的框架。

但据《纽约时报》报道，Olah 过去一年大部分时间都在召集来自各宗教派别的领袖开会。
该报形容这位34岁人士“带着孩子气”，却有着“传道者般的热忱”，据报道他正在探索道德与人工智能之间的关系。
他此前曾负责 OpenAI 的互操作性研究，再往前是 Google Brain 的研究科学家。
这名加拿大人提早离开了多伦多大学，但后来获得了 10 万美元的 Thiel Fellowship，这是一项帮助有天赋的人在没有学位的情况下进入研究领域的奖学金。
Sam McCandlish

麦坎德利什是 Anthropic 的首席架构师，帮助制定并落实该公司旨在降低人工智能风险的政策。在此之前，他曾在 OpenAI 从事安全工作。
他拥有斯坦福大学物理学博士学位，以及波士顿郊外布兰迪斯大学的数学和物理学学位。

items.title: Russian arrested for spying on US defence company Palantir over Ukraine support
items.summary: The suspect followed employees and was found with fake US IDs and two Russian passports, prosecutors say.
items.body:
Image source, US Department of Justice

Image caption,

The alleged foreign agent was discovered with two Russian passports

ByMax Matza

US investigators have arrested a Russian man who they say was recruited by Moscow to spy on employees of a technology and defence firm in California's Silicon Valley that has links to Ukraine.

Igor D'iu is accused of acting as an agent of a foreign government to conduct a spying operation in Palo Alto, near San Francisco.

He is also accused of stalking employees of the company and possessing falsified identity documents.

The company is not named in charging documents, but is described as a publicly traded technology and defence company that produces software used by Ukraine in its war with Russia. US prosecutors say the company was targeted by Russia due to its assistance to Kyiv.

"The allegations in this case describe a state-sponsored operation to target and harass employees of an American technology and defense company because of that company's assistance to Ukraine in its war with Russia," said US Attorney for the Northern District of California Craig Missakian.

"We will not tolerate any efforts - by foreign governments or otherwise - to turn Silicon Valley into a base for foreign intelligence operations."

Prosecutors say that D'iu entered the US unlawfully via the Mexico border, after travelling there from Istanbul in June.

He was allegedly recruited through the Telegram encrypted messaging app. His handlers referred to Russia as "'the Motherland' and directed D'iu to gather information about the company because it was supplying weapons used against Russia in Ukraine".

On their instruction, he purchased computers, phones, wireless networking equipment and remote access software - tools he needed for his spy mission.

He then went to a coffee shop located near the company's offices in Palo Alto, where he photographed laptop screens of employees who were working there.

His handlers also allegedly "instructed him to position his laptop at designated locations near the company so they could remotely access it and attempt to collect information from company employees in the vicinity".

Image source, US Department of Justice

Image caption,

The suspect allegedly took photos of employees screens at a cafe near the office

According to CBS News, the BBC's US partner, the company in question is Palantir Technologies. Palantir did not reply to a BBC request for comment.

D'iu also allegedly conducted surveillance of employees and their residences.

On 3 September, he followed a vehicle driven by one senior executive for nearly 30 miles. He fled after she drove to a police station. Police later obtained evidence that he had followed other employees' cars on previous days.

During the investigation, officials discovered identity cards that had been falsified - including a US passport, California ID card, and a Social Security card with the fake name "Hugo Landry Johns".

A raid on his home in October in East Palo Alto turned up two Russian passports, and a handwritten notebook that contained numerous home addresses of employees "family members' names, educational and employment histories, and assessments of their strengths and weaknesses", prosecutors say.

He faces two charges related his alleged work as a foreign agent, one charge of interstate stalking, and one count of fraud related to his identity documents. He faces over 15 years in prison if found guilty.

Image source, US Department of Justice

Image caption,

The suspect was found with forged identification documents including a US passport

He has been held in jail since 2 November. It is unclear whether he has hired a lawyer who can speak on his behalf.

The arrest comes as espionage allegations roil the US tech industry, amid the news that Nvidia ex-CEO Jensen Huang had a romantic affair with a woman suspected of spying for China.

Last month, a former OpenAI employee was charged with planting a listening device in a company office. The man was later accused of having "considerable support" from the Saudi government.

这名涉嫌外国特工被发现持有两本俄罗斯护照
作者：Max Matza
美国调查人员逮捕了一名俄罗斯男子，称其受莫斯科招募，在加利福尼亚州硅谷一家与乌克兰有关联的科技和防务公司监视员工。
Igor D'iu 被指控充当外国政府代理人，在旧金山附近的帕洛阿尔托开展间谍活动。
他还被指控跟踪该公司员工，并持有伪造的身份文件。
该公司在起诉文件中未被点名，但被描述为一家上市的科技与防务公司，其生产的软件被乌克兰用于对俄战争。美国检方称，该公司因向基辅提供帮助而成为俄罗斯的目标。
加利福尼亚北区联邦检察官克雷格·米萨基安说：“本案中的指控描述了一项由国家支持的行动，针对并骚扰一家美国科技与防务公司的员工，原因是该公司在乌克兰对俄战争中向乌克兰提供了协助。”
“我们不会容忍任何企图——无论是外国政府还是其他方面——把硅谷变成外国情报活动基地的行为。”
检方称，D'iu 于 6 月从伊斯坦布尔出发，经墨西哥边境非法进入美国。
据称他是通过加密通讯应用Telegram被招募的。他的上线称俄罗斯为“祖国”，并指示D'iu收集该公司的信息，因为它在向用于对抗俄罗斯的乌克兰战争提供武器。
按照他们的指示，他购买了电脑、手机、无线网络设备和远程访问软件——这些都是他执行间谍任务所需的工具。
随后他去了该公司帕洛阿尔托办公地点附近的一家咖啡店，在那里拍摄了正在工作的员工的笔记本电脑屏幕。
他的上线还被指“指示他把笔记本电脑放在公司附近指定地点，以便他们远程访问，并试图收集附近公司员工的信息”。

D'iu 还被指对员工及其住所进行监视。
9 月 3 日，他跟踪一名高管驾驶的车辆近 30 英里。她把车开到警察局后，他逃离了。警方后来获得证据，表明他在此前几天也曾跟踪其他员工的车辆。

他面临两项与被指控从事外国代理人工作有关的指控、一项跨州跟踪指控，以及一项与身份文件有关的欺诈罪名。若被定罪，他面临超过 15 年监禁。

Jovenel Moïse in Port-au-Prince in 2020. Haiti has not had a president since he was killed in July 2021. Photograph: Dieu Nalio Chery/AP

Florida pastor found guilty over 2021 assassination of Haitian president

Christian Emmanuel Sanon faces life in prison after conviction on charges arising from killing of Jovenel Moïse

A Florida pastor with dual Haitian-American citizenship was convicted on Wednesday of US charges arising from the 2021 assassination of the Haitian president Jovenel Moïse.

Christian Emmanuel Sanon was found guilty on charges including conspiring to kill Moïse after a nearly eight-week trial in federal court in Miami. He had faced a total of eight charges including conspiracy to kidnap or kill a person outside the United States.

He faces up to life in prison at sentencing.

Federal prosecutors said south Florida was a hub for planning and financing the plot to oust Moïse and install a president of the conspirators’ choosing. The government said Sanon was the conspirators’ initial choice for Moïse’s replacement. Prosecutors also said Sanon helped raise money for the conspiracy and arranged travel to Haiti and lodging for himself and others in that country.

Sanon acknowledged in trial testimony that he was in communication at one point with people trying to replace Moïse, but pointed out that the group had moved on to another candidate long before the assassination. He denied any knowledge of plans to kill Moïse.

Sanon was born in Haiti and moved to the US as a teenager. He testified that he worked with churches in Haitian immigrant communities in Florida and the midwest.

Haiti has not had a president since authorities said that a squad of mostly retired Colombian soldiers killed Moïse and wounded his wife in a night-time raid at their home on 7 July 2021. The poorest country in the Americas, Haiti has a history of dictatorship, political upheaval and foreign intervention that has long hindered democratic rule.

The election of a new president is scheduled for next year.

Prosecutors said the scheme to kill Moïse included paying about two dozen foreign mercenaries with money obtained from US government programs that were intended to help businesses during the Covid pandemic, according to court records. US prosecutors have charged more than 40 people with crimes related to the assassination and a dozen have been convicted, including five who are serving life sentences.

The plot to oust Moïse began taking final shape in April 2021, when Sanon met in south Florida with a former Haitian senator and several US businesspeople, according to an indictment. The group agreed that Sanon, once in power, would award contracts to two Florida-based companies – Counter Terrorist Unit Federal Academy and Counter Terrorist Unit Security, collectively known as CTU – for infrastructure projects, security forces and military equipment, according to investigators.

CTU initially hired about 18 Colombian nationals with military training to provide security for Sanon, according to prosecutors. Conspirators also spent months obtaining weapons and body armor and attempting to build ties with Haitian gangs, officials said.

By June 2021, the conspirators realized Sanon had neither the constitutional qualifications nor sufficient popular support to become president. They shifted their support to Wendelle Coq Thélot, a former Haitian supreme court judge who died in January 2025 while a fugitive.

Sanon was previously scheduled to be tried with four other men who were convicted earlier this year, but his case was separated from theirs and delayed for health reasons.

Christian Emmanuel Sanon faces life in prison after conviction on charges arising from killing of Jovenel Moïse
A Florida pastor with dual Haitian-American citizenship was convicted on Wednesday of US charges arising from the 2021 assassination of the Haitian president Jovenel Moïse.

Christian Emmanuel Sanon was found guilty on charges including conspiring to kill Moïse after a nearly eight-week trial in federal court in Miami. He had faced a total of eight charges including conspiracy to kidnap or kill a person outside the United States.
He faces up to life in prison at sentencing.

Federal prosecutors said south Florida was a hub for planning and financing the plot to oust Moïse and install a president of the conspirators’ choosing. The government said Sanon was the conspirators’ initial choice for Moïse’s replacement. Prosecutors also said Sanon helped raise money for the conspiracy and arranged travel to Haiti and lodging for himself and others in that country.

Sanon acknowledged in trial testimony that he was in communication at one point with people trying to replace Moïse, but pointed out that the group had moved on to another candidate long before the assassination. He denied any knowledge of plans to kill Moïse.
Sanon was born in Haiti and moved to the US as a teenager. He testified that he worked with churches in Haitian immigrant communities in Florida and the midwest.

Haiti has not had a president since authorities said that a squad of mostly retired Colombian soldiers killed Moïse and wounded his wife in a night-time raid at their home on 7 July 2021. The poorest country in the Americas, Haiti has a history of dictatorship, political upheaval and foreign intervention that has long hindered democratic rule.
The election of a new president is scheduled for next year.

Prosecutors said the scheme to kill Moïse included paying about two dozen foreign mercenaries with money obtained from US government programs that were intended to help businesses during the Covid pandemic, according to court records. US prosecutors have charged more than 40 people with crimes related to the assassination and a dozen have been convicted, including five who are serving life sentences.

The plot to oust Moïse began taking final shape in April 2021, when Sanon met in south Florida with a former Haitian senator and several US businesspeople, according to an indictment. The group agreed that Sanon, once in power, would award contracts to two Florida-based companies – Counter Terrorist Unit Federal Academy and Counter Terrorist Unit Security, collectively known as CTU – for infrastructure projects, security forces and military equipment, according to investigators.

CTU initially hired about 18 Colombian nationals with military training to provide security for Sanon, according to prosecutors. Conspirators also spent months obtaining weapons and body armor and attempting to build ties with Haitian gangs, officials said.

By June 2021, the conspirators realized Sanon had neither the constitutional qualifications nor sufficient popular support to become president. They shifted their support to Wendelle Coq Thélot, a former Haitian supreme court judge who died in January 2025 while a fugitive.
Sanon was previously scheduled to be tried with four other men who were convicted earlier this year, but his case was separated from theirs and delayed for health reasons.

Christian Emmanuel Sanon 因与杀害若韦内尔·莫伊兹有关的指控被定罪，面临终身监禁
一名拥有海地和美国双重国籍的佛罗里达牧师周三被判犯有与 2021 年海地总统若韦内尔·莫伊兹遇刺案相关的美国指控。
经过迈阿密联邦法院近八周的审理，Christian Emmanuel Sanon 被判定有罪，罪名包括密谋杀害 Moïse。他共面临八项指控，其中包括密谋在美国境外绑架或杀害他人。
他在量刑时最高可能面临终身监禁。
联邦检察官说，南佛罗里达是策划和资助推翻 Moïse、并扶植共谋者所选总统的阴谋的枢纽。检方称，Sanon 是共谋者最初选定的 Moïse 继任者。检察官还说，Sanon 帮助为该阴谋筹款，并安排了自己和其他人前往海地的行程及在该国的住宿。

Sanon 出生于海地，少年时移居美国。他作证说，曾在佛罗里达和中西部的海地移民社区与教会合作。
自当局称一支主要由退役哥伦比亚士兵组成的小队于2021年7月7日夜袭其住所、杀死 Moïse 并打伤其妻子以来，海地一直没有总统。作为美洲最贫穷的国家，海地有着独裁、政治动荡和外国干预的历史，长期阻碍了民主统治。
新总统选举定于明年举行。

items.title: Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries to be US Speaker of the House
items.summary: The nomination sets him on the path to become the first black lawmaker to lead the chamber when Democrats take control of the House in January.
items.body:
Image source, Getty Images

ByKayla Epstein

Updated 5 minutes ago

Democrats in the US House of Representatives officially nominated Hakeem Jeffries to be Speaker, setting him on the path to become the first black lawmaker to lead the chamber.

The House will elect its new Speaker on 3 January, when the next term begins and Democrats will hold a majority of the seats.

As of Wednesday, Democrats will hold at least 257 seats in the US House next year, with seven races still uncalled.

His election to the powerful position - the Speaker is in the line of succession to the presidency after the vice-president - is widely expected.

Jeffries, who represents a district in New York, was re-elected as the party leader in a 251-11 closed-door vote on Wednesday. He has served as minority leader since 2023.

Despite overwhelming support, Jeffries faced a handful of holdouts from the party's left wing.

"While we have seen meaningful progress, there is still work to be done to ensure that the direction our party takes in this coming Congress reflects what our constituents are demanding of our leadership," seven incoming lawmakers, including fellow New Yorkers Darializa Avila Chevalier and Claire Valdez, said in a statement.

items.body:
Pete Hegseth gives a press conference at the US Embassy in Caracas on 18 November. Photograph: Juan Barreto/AFP/Getty Images

Pete Hegseth gives a press conference at the US Embassy in Caracas on 18 November. Photograph: Juan Barreto/AFP/Getty Images

Hegseth boasts of Maduro’s capture while vowing to deepen US military cooperation with Venezuela

The US defense secretary called the former president’s capture the ‘most sophisticated military operation’ in Latin American history

Pete Hegseth has used his first visit to Venezuela since US special forces abducted its former president, Nicolás Maduro, to boast of the dictator’s capture during what he called “the single most sophisticated military operation in the history of Latin America”.

Maduro was controversially seized by Delta Force operatives in the early hours of 3 January, setting in motion an improbable rapprochement between Washington and Venezuela’s anti-imperialist “Chavista” regime, which has ruled since 1999.

Speaking outside the recently reopened US embassy in Venezuela’s capital, Caracas, on Wednesday, Hegseth said: “It’s a great honor to be here as the first United States secretary of war this century to set foot in Venezuela.​ Just one year ago my presence here … would have been deemed impossible, almost unimaginable.

“In fact, exactly one year ago today … [Maduro] stood on a stage not too far from here and yelled mockingly, ‘Come and get me!’” Hegseth recalled, before adding sarcastically: “Well, we answered that call.

“The reality is that … January 3 is the day that will go down in history as a day of liberation for Venezuela,” Hegseth claimed, although Maduro’s allies continue to hold power with US support.

Earlier in the day, Hegseth was welcomed to the Miraflores Palace by Maduro’s former vice-president, Delcy Rodríguez, who became acting president with Donald Trump’s blessing after his abduction.

In the aftermath of the deadly US attack, Hegseth was one of the bluntest Trump administration voices when it came to celebrating the invasion. “Maduro had his chance … he effed around and he found out,” the defense secretary bragged.

Speaking at the palace, Hegseth struck a more conciliatory tone as he vowed to deepen cooperation with Venezuela’s new leaders in brief comments that were broadcast by the state broadcaster VTV.

“I stand here on behalf of President Trump, who sends his greeting and looks forward to the opportunities, not just militarily … but also economically: the incredible resource capabilities that your country has, that we look forward to unlocking together with you,” Hegseth told Rodríguez and senior cabinet members, including the defense and foreign ministers, Gustavo González López and Oliver Blanco.

Hegseth said his visit to Rodríguez’s “beautiful country” was designed to re-establish and increase “defense cooperation” between “two great militaries” that less than a year ago were briefly at war. Earlier this month, the New York Times reported that Trump officials were trying to negotiate a long-term US troop presence in Venezuela as part of their push for regional hegemony.

“I appreciate your leadership and commitment to your country,” Hegseth told Maduro’s successor, a once outspoken anti-imperialist leftist who has overseen an unlikely realignment with Washington since her ally was grabbed.

During her five-minute address, Rodríguez, whose oil-rich country is widely seen to have become a US protectorate after January’s invasion, made no mention of Maduro, who is behind bars in New York City.

But referring indirectly to his capture and the subsequent reconciliation with Washington, she told Hegseth: “Thanks to the political and geopolitical maturity of our governments, we have – in a very short period of time, just a few months – turned what were very difficult and very tough times for our people, into an extraordinary space for cooperation and mutual benefit.”

Rodríguez hailed the “historic” energy deal her government recently struck with Trump, who has called it “the biggest oil deal in world history” as well as “the spoils” of his “conquest” of Venezuela.

Hegseth claimed the agreement, which reportedly involves 65bn barrels of reserves, “makes the strait of Hormuz a non-factor for the western hemisphere”.

Critics of Rodríguez’s political movement painted Hegseth’s visit as a humiliating act of genuflection for a president with no choice but to roll out the red carpet for the man whose troops captured her boss.

Writing on X, Luz Mely Reyes, a prominent Venezuelan journalist, said Hegseth’s visit was designed to underscore Washington’s “direct administration” of her country.

“Ten months after Nicolás Maduro’s capture, Washington no longer needs to fire shots to remind everyone who is in charge: the mere presence on Venezuelan soil of the architect of the January incursion reaffirms that the country’s operational sovereignty is subject to the White House’s directives,” Reyes said.

Reyes suspected the visit also carried a message for members of Venezuela’s armed forces. “Domestically, the trip forces the military high command to legitimize the man who directed the extraction of their former commander in chief,” she said. “In this regard, I wonder whether it might be a message of discipline intended to prevent any pockets of resistance in the barracks.”

Trump’s attempts to expand his Shield of the Americas anti-cartel coalition of Latin American governments suffered a major blow last month with the defeat of his far-right ally, Flávio Bolsonaro, in Brazil’s presidential election. The leftwing winner, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has indicated his country will not join the initiative.

But Venezuela’s interim government is in little position to resist. During his surprise visit to Venezuela, Hegseth said Venezuela had gone from being “our most aggressive regional threat to [being] a compliant security partner”. He praised Rodríguez for working “closely, pragmatically, and diligently with the United States to stabilize Venezuela”. Hegseth claimed US and Venezuelan armed forces would work together to attack “narco-terrorists” operating on Venezuelan soil, vowing: “We will hunt you down. We will find you. And we will kill you.”

Concluding her speech at the palace, Rodríguez told her foe-turned-friend: “Thank you, secretary, and I wish you a lifetime of happiness.”

blocks.text: 皮特·赫格塞斯 11 月 18 日在加拉加斯美国大使馆举行新闻发布会。照片：Juan Barreto/AFP/Getty Images
皮特·赫格塞斯 11 月 18 日在加拉加斯美国大使馆举行新闻发布会。照片：Juan Barreto/AFP/Getty Images
赫格塞斯夸耀抓获马杜罗，同时誓言深化美国与委内瑞拉的军事合作
美国国防部长称，抓获这位前总统是拉美历史上“最复杂的军事行动”
自美国特种部队绑架委内瑞拉前总统尼古拉斯·马杜罗以来，皮特·赫格塞斯首次访问该国，并借此吹嘘这次对独裁者的抓捕，称之为「拉丁美洲历史上最精密的一次军事行动」。
马杜罗于 1 月 3 日凌晨被 Delta Force 人员颇具争议地抓获，由此开启了华盛顿与自 1999 年以来统治委内瑞拉的反帝「查韦斯派」政权之间一场出人意料的和解。
周三，Hegseth 在刚重新开放的美国驻委内瑞拉首都加拉加斯大使馆外说：“作为本世纪第一位踏上委内瑞拉土地的美国战争部长，我深感荣幸。就在一年前，我出现在这里……还会被认为是不可能的，几乎无法想象。”
“事实上，整整一年前的今天……[马杜罗]就站在离这里不远的舞台上，嘲讽地喊道：‘来抓我啊！’”赫格塞斯回忆说，然后挖苦地补充道：“好吧，我们回应了那一声召唤。
“现实是……1 月 3 日将成为载入史册的一天，是委内瑞拉的解放日，”Hegseth 声称，尽管 Maduro 的盟友在美国支持下继续掌权。
当天早些时候，Hegseth 在米拉弗洛雷斯宫受到 Maduro 前副总统 Delcy Rodríguez 的欢迎；在 Maduro 被绑架后，她在 Donald Trump 的祝福下成为代总统。
在这场造成人员死亡的美国袭击之后，Hegseth 是特朗普政府中最直言不讳地庆祝这次入侵的声音之一。「马杜罗本来有机会……他作死，就遭到了报应，」这位国防部长吹嘘说。
在总统府发表讲话时，Hegseth 的语气更为和解，他誓言将深化与委内瑞拉新领导人的合作；这番简短评论由官方电视台 VTV 播出。
“我代表特朗普总统站在这里，他向你们致意，并期待各种机会，不仅是军事上的……还有经济上的：贵国拥有令人难以置信的资源能力，我们期待与你们一起释放它们，”Hegseth 对 Rodríguez 以及包括国防部长和外交部长 Gustavo González López 和 Oliver Blanco 在内的高级内阁成员说。
Hegseth 说，他访问 Rodríguez 的“美丽国家”，是为了在“两支伟大的军队”之间重新建立并加强“防务合作”，而就在不到一年前，双方还曾短暂交战。本月早些时候，《纽约时报》报道称，特朗普政府官员正试图谈判美军在委内瑞拉的长期驻留，作为其推动地区霸权的一部分。
「我赞赏你的领导力和对国家的担当，」Hegseth 对马杜罗的继任者说道。她曾是直言不讳的反帝左翼人士，却在盟友被抓后主导了与华盛顿之间一场出人意料的重新站队。
在五分钟的讲话中，罗德里格斯没有提及被关押在纽约市的马杜罗。她所在的这个石油资源丰富的国家，在今年1月的入侵之后被普遍视为已变成美国的保护国。
但在间接提到他被抓获以及随后与华盛顿和解时，她对 Hegseth 说：“多亏我们两国政府在政治和地缘政治上的成熟，我们在很短的时间里——仅仅几个月——就把对我们人民而言非常艰难、非常严酷的时期，转变成了合作与互利的非凡空间。”
Rodríguez 盛赞其政府最近与 Trump 达成的“历史性”能源协议；Trump 称之为“世界历史上最大的石油交易”，也是他“征服”委内瑞拉的“战利品”。
赫格塞斯声称，这项据报涉及 650 亿桶储量的协议，“让霍尔木兹海峡对西半球不再构成影响因素”。
罗德里格斯政治运动的批评者将赫格塞斯的访问描绘成一种屈辱的跪拜：一位别无选择的总统，只能为率军逮捕其上司的那个人铺上红地毯。
著名委内瑞拉记者卢斯·梅利·雷耶斯在 X 上写道，赫格塞斯此行是为了凸显华盛顿对她的国家的“直接管理”。
Reyes 说：“在 Nicolás Maduro 被捕十个月后，华盛顿已无需再开枪来提醒所有人谁说了算：这位一月份军事行动的策划者现身委内瑞拉领土本身，就再次表明该国的行动主权受白宫指令约束。”
Reyes 怀疑此次访问也向委内瑞拉武装部队成员传递了信息。“在国内，这次行程迫使军方高层去承认那个指挥了前总司令被带走行动的人，”她说。“在这一点上，我在想，这会不会是一条旨在防止军营中出现任何抵抗据点的纪律信息。”
特朗普扩大其“美洲之盾”拉美政府反卡特尔联盟的努力上个月遭受重大打击，其极右翼盟友弗拉维奥·博尔索纳罗在巴西总统选举中落败。左翼胜选者路易斯·伊纳西奥·卢拉·达席尔瓦已表明，他的国家不会加入该倡议。
但委内瑞拉的临时政府几乎没有能力抵抗。Hegseth 在突然访问委内瑞拉时说，委内瑞拉已经从「我们在该地区最具侵略性的威胁，变成了合规的安全伙伴」。他称赞 Rodríguez「与美国密切、务实、勤勉地合作，以稳定委内瑞拉」。Hegseth 声称美国和委内瑞拉武装力量将共同打击在委内瑞拉境内活动的「毒枭恐怖分子」，并誓言：「我们会追查你们。我们会找到你们。我们会杀掉你们。」
罗德里格斯在王宫演讲结束时对这位由敌转友的对象说：“谢谢你，部长，祝你一生幸福。”

items.summary: The meeting in New Delhi was a late addition to the royal couple's India visit, which also included their appearance at the annual Earthshot Prize
items.body:
Image source, Andrew Parsons / Kensington Palace

ByHenry Moore

Updated 1 hour ago

The Prince and Princess of Wales have met Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi as part of their three-day visit to India.

William and Catherine arrived in New Dehli on Wednesday for the final leg of their first official oversees trip together in four years.

The meeting was a late addition to the couple's schedule and came after Modi confirmed he would be back from a scheduled trip to the Philippines in time to see the royals.

It comes a day after the royal couple were in Mumbai for the annual Earthshot Prize, which was founded by the prince and remains one of his biggest personal projects.

• Street cricket with a legend then metro ride as William and Kate begin India visitPublished2 days ago

When he announced earlier this year that it was going to be held in India for the first time, the prince highlighted India's leadership in climate innovation, its biodiversity and its massive youth population as the key reasons for choosing the country.

A Kensington Palace spokesperson said ahead of the Modi meeting: "For the Prince, it represents another significant engagement as he continues to take on a growing role on the international stage,

"We've seen him increasingly support the UK's diplomatic relationships through his overseas engagements, and this meeting will provide an opportunity to build on those connections at the highest level."

The couple last met Modi on their official visit to India in 2016.

Image source, EPA

On Tuesday the prince and princess were in Mumbai to announce the winners of the annual Earthshot Prize.

The event, founded by Prince William in 2020, was hosted by Karan Johar, presenter of The Traitors India and one of the country's most well-known film makers.

Five separate winners were named during Tuesday's ceremony and each will receive £1m to scale up their projects.

Speaking at the ceremony, Prince William said the 2020s were the time when positive change becomes "irreversible", adding history was "not written by challenges alone", but also by those who rose to meet them.

The princess presented on the five awards and, as she did so, said the entrepreneurs, organisations and scientists tackling the environmental crisis brought her "hope".

Inside the old gas pipeline where Ukraine is fighting an underground war with Russia

Inside the old gas pipeline where Ukraine is fighting an underground war with Russia

For the past seven months Ukrainian forces have been living and fighting Russian troops in an old Soviet gas pipeline in the Kharkiv region.

The BBC is the first international broadcaster to enter the pipeline where this subterranean battle is taking place.

With a diameter of just over a metre there's enough room only to crawl. But it is relatively safe from the drones that now saturate the skies above the front line – and which are making it nigh-on impossible for either side to advance.

The BBC's defence correspondent Jonathan Beale reports from near Kupyansk, where he went underground with the 13th Khartiia Operational Brigade.

items.title: Julio Iglesias facing court investigation over alleged sexual offences
items.summary: The 83-year-old singer is accused of abusing two former employees at Caribbean residences in 2021.
items.body:
Image source, Getty Images

ByAmy Walker

Singer Julio Iglesias is facing an investigation by Spain's national court over allegations he sexually abused and assaulted two female former staff members

Two women, who worked for the 83-year-old in the Caribbean, have accused him of abuse which they say took place in the Bahamas and the Dominican Republic in 2021.

The announcement comes after Spanish prosecutors dropped an inquiry into the claims earlier this year after concluding that they lacked jurisdiction because the alleged crimes took place abroad.

Iglesias, who has been a household name in Spain since the 1960s and has sold millions of records worldwide, has previously denied the allegations.

But in a statement published on Wednesday, external (in Spanish), national court Judge Antonio Piña said the account given in the complaint, alongside preliminary evidence provided, justified opening criminal proceedings.

He added that the investigation would cover parts of the complaint relating to potential crimes against sexual freedom, as well as assault and degrading treatment.

But the court will not investigate claims made in the lawsuit of human trafficking or crimes against workers' rights. Piña said these allegations were dismissed after the he looked into the hiring of the women and found there was "no deception or artifice involved".

Piña said the former employees had been summoned to testify in person on 3 February.

The announcement comes after Spain's public prosecutor's office shifted its position last month, saying it now believed the court had jurisdiction to investigate the allegations.

In its statement, the national court said Spanish law sets out that courts can hear cases of crimes committed abroad by Spanish citizens provided certain conditions are met.

The allegations against Iglesias first emerged in a joint three-year investigation between Spanish newspaper El Diario, external and television network Univision news, published in January.

In that investigation, the two women were identified as a domestic worker and a physical therapist, who described alleged sexual abuse and degrading working conditions.

The domestic worker, whose name was changed to Rebeca in the reports, said Iglesias would regularly call her to his room at the end of the day and would touch her inappropriately without consent.

Rebeca, a Dominican who was 22 when the alleged events took place, also alleged that Iglesias had forced her to take part in threesomes with another female member of staff. She also described the singer slapping her in the face and grabbing her genitals.

The other woman, a Venezuelan physical therapist named as Laura in the article, said Iglesias had touched her breasts and kissed her on the mouth against her will. She added that he constantly threatened to fire her, controlled how much food she ate and asked her about when her period was due.

Rebeca and Laura filed an initial legal complaint in January against Iglesias for sexual assault and human trafficking.

In a response to the allegations in January, Iglesias said, external: "I deny having abused, coerced, or disrespected any woman. These accusations are absolutely false and deeply sadden me."

On Wednesday, the court said the lawsuit had been accepted based on evidence provided in the complaint. This included a photograph of one of the complainants, showing a bruise on her arm that was "consistent with the possibility of her being grabbed forcefully".

It added that the same photo showed "two marks on one of her thighs that could correspond to a human bite", which the complainant said were "a consequence of her forced participation in acts of a sexual nature".

WhatsApp message exchanges, including New Year's greetings, which suggest an "affectionate" relationship between the women and Iglesias, will also be considered, the court said.

But it added that the seemingly cordial tone, which presents "an apparent discrepancy with certain aspects of the narrative", would be clarified through a "complete and contextualised examination of the communications".

The claim over violations of workers' rights could not be investigated because there is no comparable criminal offence in the Bahamas and the Dominican Republic, where the alleged crimes took place, it said.

Iglesias is one of the most successful Latin artists of all time, having sold more than 300 million records in a career spanning decades.

He is also the father of fellow music superstar Enrique Iglesias.

In its statement, the national court said Spanish law sets out that courts can hear cases of crimes committed abroad by Spanish citizens provided certain conditions are met.
The allegations against Iglesias first emerged in a joint three-year investigation between Spanish newspaper El Diario, external and television network Univision news, published in January.
In that investigation, the two women were identified as a domestic worker and a physical therapist, who described alleged sexual abuse and degrading working conditions.
The domestic worker, whose name was changed to Rebeca in the reports, said Iglesias would regularly call her to his room at the end of the day and would touch her inappropriately without consent.

Rebeca, a Dominican who was 22 when the alleged events took place, also alleged that Iglesias had forced her to take part in threesomes with another female member of staff. She also described the singer slapping her in the face and grabbing her genitals.

The other woman, a Venezuelan physical therapist named as Laura in the article, said Iglesias had touched her breasts and kissed her on the mouth against her will. She added that he constantly threatened to fire her, controlled how much food she ate and asked her about when her period was due.
Rebeca and Laura filed an initial legal complaint in January against Iglesias for sexual assault and human trafficking.
In a response to the allegations in January, Iglesias said, external: "I deny having abused, coerced, or disrespected any woman. These accusations are absolutely false and deeply sadden me."

On Wednesday, the court said the lawsuit had been accepted based on evidence provided in the complaint. This included a photograph of one of the complainants, showing a bruise on her arm that was "consistent with the possibility of her being grabbed forcefully".

It added that the same photo showed "two marks on one of her thighs that could correspond to a human bite", which the complainant said were "a consequence of her forced participation in acts of a sexual nature".
WhatsApp message exchanges, including New Year's greetings, which suggest an "affectionate" relationship between the women and Iglesias, will also be considered, the court said.

But it added that the seemingly cordial tone, which presents "an apparent discrepancy with certain aspects of the narrative", would be clarified through a "complete and contextualised examination of the communications".

The claim over violations of workers' rights could not be investigated because there is no comparable criminal offence in the Bahamas and the Dominican Republic, where the alleged crimes took place, it said.
Iglesias is one of the most successful Latin artists of all time, having sold more than 300 million records in a career spanning decades.
He is also the father of fellow music superstar Enrique Iglesias.

歌手 Julio Iglesias 因涉嫌性虐待和性侵两名前女性工作人员，正面临西班牙国家法院的调查
两名曾在加勒比地区为这名83岁男子工作的女性指控他实施虐待，称事件发生在2021年的巴哈马和多米尼加共和国。
此番宣布是在西班牙检察官今年早些时候终止对这些指控的调查之后作出的，检方当时认为他们没有管辖权，因为所谓犯罪发生在国外。
自上世纪60年代以来就在西班牙家喻户晓、全球唱片销量达数百万的 Iglesias，此前已否认这些指控。
但在周三公布的一份声明（西班牙文）中，国家法院法官 Antonio Piña 表示，诉状中的陈述连同所提供的初步证据，足以构成启动刑事程序的理由。
他补充说，调查将涵盖投诉中涉及可能侵犯性自由的罪名，以及伤害和有辱人格待遇的部分。
但法院不会调查诉状中提出的人口贩运或侵犯工人权利的指控。Piña 说，这些指控在他审查了这些女性的雇佣情况后被驳回，因为他发现「不存在欺骗或诡计」。
Piña 说，前雇员已接到传唤，将于 2 月 3 日亲自出庭作证。
此番宣布是在西班牙检察官办公室上个月改变立场之后作出的，检方现在认为法院有权调查这些指控。
国家法院在声明中表示，西班牙法律规定，在满足特定条件的情况下，法院可以审理西班牙公民在国外实施的犯罪案件。
针对 Iglesias 的指控最初出现在西班牙报纸 El Diario（external）与电视网 Univision news 为期三年的联合调查中，并于1月发表。
在那次调查中，两名女性被确认为一名家政工和一名物理治疗师，她们描述了据称遭受的性虐待和有辱人格的工作条件。
这名家政工在报道中被改名为 Rebeca，她说 Iglesias 会经常在一天结束时把她叫到自己房间，并在未经同意的情况下对她进行不适当的触碰。
丽贝卡是多米尼加人，所称事件发生时她22岁，她还指控伊格莱西亚斯强迫她与另一名女性工作人员参与三人行。她还描述这名歌手掴她耳光并抓她的私处。
另一名女性是文章中称为劳拉的委内瑞拉物理治疗师，她说伊格莱西亚斯曾在违背其意愿的情况下触碰她的胸部并亲吻她的嘴。她还说，他不断威胁要解雇她，控制她的进食量，并询问她月经何时到来。
丽贝卡和劳拉于 1 月对伊格莱西亚斯提出初步法律投诉，指控其性侵和人口贩运。
针对这些指控，Iglesias 在 1 月的回应中对外表示：“我否认曾虐待、胁迫或不尊重任何女性。这些指控完全不实，令我深感痛心。”
周三，法院表示已根据诉状中提供的证据受理该诉讼。证据包括其中一名原告的照片，显示其手臂上有淤伤，「与可能遭到强力抓握相符」。
它还称，同一张照片显示“她一侧大腿上有两处痕迹，可能对应人类咬痕”，投诉人说这些是“她被迫参与性质为性的行为的后果”。
法院表示，还将审阅 WhatsApp 消息往来，包括新年问候，这些内容表明这些女性与伊格莱西亚斯之间存在“亲昵”关系。
但它补充说，这种看似友好的语气呈现出“与叙述中某些方面的明显出入”，将通过对这些通信进行“完整且结合语境的审查”来澄清。
它表示，有关侵犯工人权利的指控无法调查，因为在据称罪行发生地巴哈马和多米尼加共和国，没有相应的刑事罪名。
伊格莱西亚斯是有史以来最成功的拉丁艺人之一，数十年职业生涯中唱片销量超过3亿张。
他也是同为音乐巨星的 Enrique Iglesias 的父亲。
